Data Classification and Governance Policy
Meridian Capital
Policy ID: MC-EDO-DCG-001 | Version: 3.2 | Effective Date: 2026-07-01 | Review Cycle: 12 months
Owning Team: Enterprise Data Office (EDO) | Co-stewards: Security Governance & Assurance (SG&A), Legal & Compliance (L&C), Privacy Office (PO)
Approval: Data Governance Council (DGC) Minute Ref: DGC-2026-07-01-04 | Executive Sponsor: Chief Data Officer (CDO)
Document Record: Confluence DOC-019283 | Jira Epics: EDO-1345, EDO-1522 | ServiceNow Change: CHG0054832 | Audit Ref: IA-26-071

1. Policy Overview and Purpose
This Data Classification and Governance Policy establishes the enterprise standard for classifying, labeling, and governing data assets across Meridian Capital. It defines consistent taxonomies, stakeholder accountabilities, and oversight mechanisms necessary to ensure that data is handled in accordance with legal, regulatory, contractual, and internal control requirements. The policy is a pillar of Meridian Capital’s Information Governance Framework and directly supports enterprise objectives for risk reduction, regulatory compliance, operational efficiency, and data enablement. The policy supersedes MC-EDO-DCG-001 v3.1 (effective 2025-06-30), incorporating enhancements derived from quarterly operational reviews, Internal Audit IA-25-317 follow-ups, and the Data Stewardship Council (DSC) workplan item DSC-2026-Q2-07.

The scope and intent of this policy are deliberately comprehensive: to make data classification a default characteristic of all enterprise data assets; to embed stewardship and accountability within business domains; and to ensure that classification decisions are verifiable, consistently applied, and measurable. The policy leverages a unified classification framework, integrating legal and regulatory obligations (e.g., GLBA, SOX, GDPR, CCPA) with Meridian Capital’s risk appetite, control environment, and client commitments.

2. Scope and Applicability
This policy applies enterprise-wide to all data assets created, received, processed, transmitted, accessed, or retained by Meridian Capital, including structured datasets, unstructured documents, semi-structured files, logs, models, derived datasets, and reference/master data. Applicability extends to data in all states (in motion, at rest, and in use) and across all hosting models, including on-premises data centers, managed services, and public cloud platforms under Technology Operations (TechOps) and Cloud Platform Services (CPS) oversight. The policy covers all business units, subsidiaries, and controlled joint ventures where Meridian Capital has operational control, as well as contractors and service providers handling Meridian Capital data under contractual arrangements managed by Strategic Sourcing and third-party risk management (TPRM).

The policy interfaces with—but does not duplicate—the Corporate Records Management Standard (MC-RIM-STD-002), the Privacy and Data Protection Policy (MC-PO-PDP-004), and the Information Risk Management Standard (MC-R&C-IRM-006). Where there is overlap, the most stringent applicable requirement prevails. This policy is published as “Internal Use Only” and is accessible via the Governance Repository (Confluence DOC-019283) to all authorized employees and contractors.

3. Policy Statement and Objectives
Meridian Capital requires that all enterprise data assets are classified using the standard classification taxonomy at the point of creation or acquisition and that the assigned classification is maintained as the asset evolves through its lifecycle. Classification shall be discernible, consistently applied across systems and processes, and retrievable for reporting, audit, and regulatory inquiries. The objectives of this policy are to: establish a single enterprise classification framework with clear definitions; delineate roles and responsibilities for data owners, stewards, custodians, and users; embed classification metadata within enterprise data catalogs and lineage tooling; and enable monitoring using standardized metrics and thresholds.

Outcomes are measured through key performance indicators (KPIs) reported quarterly to the DGC. Baseline metrics as of Q2 FY26 (report GSM-2026-Q2-DCG, issued 2026-06-20T10:18:54Z) indicate: 93.4% of registered data assets carry an approved classification; median time-to-classify for new assets is 6.2 business days against a 10-business-day internal target; 98.1% of stewarded domains met the quarterly review cadence; and 147 classification-related tickets remain open beyond 30 days (ServiceNow queue EDO-CLASS), trending down 12% quarter-over-quarter. These metrics inform prioritization, resourcing, and continuous improvement actions coordinated by the EDO.

4. Governance Model and Oversight
The Data Governance Council (DGC), chaired by the CDO and comprising senior representatives from Risk & Controls (R&C), SG&A, L&C, PO, TechOps, and major business lines, provides policy oversight and approves enterprise-wide changes. The Council meets monthly (standard calendar: second Wednesday, 15:00–16:30 ET) with minutes recorded under DGC Minute References and archived in DOC-010212. The Data Stewardship Council (DSC) operates as a practitioner forum, convened bi-weekly to resolve classification ambiguities, harmonize domain-specific taxonomies, and manage the steward workplan. Decisions of the DSC are recorded in Jira (component: Data Governance) and escalated to the DGC when policy interpretation or cross-domain alignment is required.

The Enterprise Data Office acts as policy owner and custodian of the classification taxonomy, coordinating inputs from business data owners, domain stewards, SG&A, and the Privacy Office. SG&A ensures alignment with enterprise control standards and provides independent assurance through control design reviews and thematic assessments. L&C and the Privacy Office interpret regulatory and contractual drivers, advising on jurisdictional nuances and client obligations. TechOps and CPS ensure classification metadata can be discovered and reported through enterprise tooling, including the data catalog, lineage, and observability platforms. Internal Audit performs periodic reviews on design and operating effectiveness, with current observations tracked under IA-26-071-DCG and managed via EDO remediation tickets (EDO-REM-320 through EDO-REM-339).

5. Definitions (Selected)
For purposes of this policy, a data asset is any collection of data elements managed as a unit, including datasets, documents, reports, dashboards, and analytical models with embedded data. A data owner is the accountable executive within a business domain who authorizes classification decisions and accepts residual risk. A data steward is the appointed subject matter expert responsible for maintaining classification accuracy and metadata quality for assigned assets. A data custodian is the technology function responsible for hosting, storing, transmitting, or integrating data assets while honoring assigned classification. A data user is any individual with authorized access to a data asset for business purposes. The classification taxonomy (Section 7) establishes the standardized labels adopted enterprise-wide.

Record of Revisions
- v3.2 (2026-07-01): Updated taxonomy definitions for cross-border data elements; refined KPI set; incorporated DGC decisions through minute ref DGC-2026-05-10-03; addressed Internal Audit observation IA-25-317-Obs2 on stewardship coverage. Change authorized under CHG0054832.
- v3.1 (2025-07-01): Introduced lineage integration requirements; established DSC charter; initial KPI baseline. Change authorized under CHG0049210.
- v3.0 (2024-07-01): Major refresh aligning with Information Governance Framework v2.0. Change authorized under CHG0041127.

6. Classification Framework Overview
Meridian Capital adopts a four-level classification framework designed to be intuitive, consistently applicable, and interoperable with regulatory regimes and client commitments. The levels are: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Public denotes data approved for broad dissemination without limiting conditions (e.g., published research summaries and corporate press releases). Internal covers routine business data intended for Meridian Capital personnel and authorized contractors, where distribution is controlled by business need. Confidential encompasses data where unauthorized disclosure could cause material harm to clients, employees, operations, or partners, including, for example, non-public financial results prior to issuance, non-public client contact details, and proprietary methodologies. Restricted applies to highly sensitive data subject to explicit legal, regulatory, contractual, or fiduciary obligations, including personal data under privacy laws, select customer financial data subject to sector regulations, and other data where loss or misuse could significantly impact clients or the firm.

The taxonomy includes auxiliary attributes to express contextual dimensions needed for compliant handling. These attributes include jurisdictional tags to signal geographic legal applicability, data subject categories (e.g., client, employee, counterparty), domain tags mapping to the Enterprise Data Domain Catalog, and retention class references aligned to Records Management (MC-RIM-STD-002). Standardized definitions are maintained by the EDO and periodically reviewed by the DSC to ensure that domain-specific examples remain current with evolving business activities and legal interpretations. Where ambiguity arises, the DSC records deliberations in Jira (EDO-DSC board), and final clarifications are reflected in the policy glossary under controlled change.

7. Data Domains and Examples
The Enterprise Data Domain Catalog organizes data into coherent business groupings for stewardship and reporting. Current domains include, without limitation: Client & Relationship, Trading & Execution, Market Data, Risk & Quantitative Analytics, Finance & Treasury, Operations & Middle Office, Human Capital, Legal & Compliance, Technology & Platforms, and Vendor & Third-Party. Typical examples include customer onboarding documents, trade confirmations, market tick data, value-at-risk outputs, general ledger balances, reconciliations, employee records, regulatory filings, system inventory metadata, and supplier due diligence packages. Each domain maintains a stewardship roster with designated owners and alternates, documented in the Steward Registry (DOC-013477), with updates tracked via ServiceNow group EDO-STEWARDS. Domains leverage the common classification levels; however, examples and rationales are tailored within each domain to promote accurate and consistent classification decisions.

As of the Q2 FY26 stewardship attestation cycle (attestation window closed 2026-06-14T23:59:00Z), 41 domains and sub-domains submitted confirmations of taxonomy adoption and catalog completeness. Two domains (Vendor & Third-Party, Operations & Middle Office) reported minor variances related to legacy repositories pending catalog integration, with remediation plans logged under EDO-REM-332 and EDO-REM-334, targeting closure before the next quarterly cycle.

8. Lifecycle Governance
Classification persists across the data lifecycle—from creation and ingestion through usage, sharing, retention, archival, and disposition—and must remain accurate as data is enriched, transformed, or aggregated. Lifecycle governance requires that classification metadata accompanies data assets in enterprise catalogs and lineage views to enable traceability of classification decisions across systems and processes. When data assets are combined or derived, the resulting classification reflects the most sensitive component and any applicable jurisdictional or contractual constraints. The Records Management function supplies retention and disposition schedules; stewards ensure that classification attributes and retention classes referenced for each asset are coherent and that catalog entries indicate the authoritative source for retention rules.

Quarterly review cadences are enforced to validate classification accuracy and metadata completeness. Reviews are scheduled in alignment with domain operating rhythms and recorded as attestations, with evidence retained in the Governance Repository for a minimum of three years to support auditability. Sampling and thematic checks are coordinated by SG&A to detect inconsistencies or drift, with outcomes reported to the DGC through the Governance Scorecard (GSM series). Where reviews identify gaps, remediation tickets are created in ServiceNow (queue: EDO-CLASS, priority assigned per impact and exposure criteria), and target dates are set by domain owners. The EDO consolidates remediation trends into a quarterly analysis to identify systemic issues, training needs, or taxonomy clarifications.

9. Roles and Responsibilities
Data owners are accountable for the classification accuracy of assets within their domain and for ensuring that stewards have the capacity and subject matter coverage necessary to perform their duties. Owners approve classification decisions, especially in ambiguous cases or where cross-border or contractual elements arise. Data stewards maintain classification metadata, monitor domain KPIs, coordinate quarterly attestations, and propose taxonomy refinements. Custodians in TechOps and CPS ensure that classification metadata is discoverable in enterprise tooling and that reporting channels can provide timely insights to stakeholders. The Privacy Office and L&C provide advisory interpretations for regulatory and contractual matters and participate in reviews where data subject to privacy or legal constraints is implicated. SG&A performs second-line oversight, administering thematic reviews and control assessments, and advising on alignment with enterprise control frameworks. All employees and authorized contractors are responsible for adhering to the assigned classification of data they use and for reporting observed discrepancies via established channels (ServiceNow catalog item: EDO-INC-CLASS).

10. Monitoring, Metrics, and Reporting
The policy’s effectiveness is measured through KPIs and key risk indicators (KRIs) maintained by the EDO and reviewed by the DGC. Core measures include percentage of cataloged assets with approved classification, time-to-classify for new assets, quarterly attestation completion rates, steward coverage ratios, and the volume and aging of classification-related tickets. KRIs track indicators such as fluctuations in Restricted data inventory, cross-border data element prevalence by jurisdiction tag, and recurring themes identified by SG&A’s sampling. The Q2 FY26 Governance Scorecard (GSM-2026-Q2-DCG) recorded a 1.3 percentage point improvement in classification coverage and a 0.4-day improvement in median time-to-classify compared to the prior quarter. Two yellow-rated KRIs remained open related to cross-domain consistency in jurisdictional tagging; corrective actions are documented in EDO-REM-335 and EDO-REM-336 with target remediation dates in Q3 FY26. Reporting is delivered to the DGC monthly and to executive management quarterly, with timestamps and distribution lists maintained for audit traceability.

This policy does not authorize exceptions. Identified gaps are remediated through standard governance channels with accountability tracked to data owners and stewards, and progress monitored by the EDO and SG&A. The absence of exceptions reinforces uniformity and predictability in governance and supports Meridian Capital’s commitment to consistent, high-quality data management across all domains.

Section 2. Governance Structure and Accountability

2.1 Oversight Bodies and Operating Model
Meridian Capital’s Data Governance operating model is anchored by a tiered structure that establishes clear decision rights, sustained executive sponsorship, and measurable accountability across business lines and enabling functions. The Enterprise Data Governance Council (EDGC) serves as the principal authority for this policy and meets on a scheduled quarterly cadence, with extraordinary sessions convened as required by material changes in regulatory expectations or strategic programs. The EDGC is chaired by the Chief Data Officer (CDO) and includes voting members from the Institutional Markets Group, Wealth Management, Finance, Risk, Operations, Legal & Compliance, and Technology. Quorum is defined as the CDO plus a minimum of four business-aligned members and one control partner (Information Risk & Compliance or Privacy Office). The EDGC charter (Ref. DGC-CHARTER-2025 v3.2) outlines remit, membership, and standard agenda items, including policy stewardship, oversight of classification coverage metrics, and disposition of material exceptions previously authorized under legacy frameworks. No new exceptions are within scope of this policy; remediation planning and closure are overseen by the EDGC until legacy gaps are retired.

Working committees report into the EDGC to provide subject matter depth and continuous operational oversight. The Data Quality Steering Group (DQSG) prioritizes remediation of data defects that have classification implications and tracks sustained improvements via lineage-informed root cause narratives. The Privacy & Records Forum ensures that classification decisions are harmonized with records retention schedules and applicable data residency requirements. The Technology Enablement Working Group (TEWG) aligns platform capabilities for cataloging and metadata with the policy’s classification needs. All committees submit monthly summaries to the EDGC Secretariat, including action items, status of open decisions, and relevant ticket references for audit traceability.

2.2 Roles and Responsibilities
Data ownership is assigned at the domain level and is held by senior business leaders (Managing Director or VP-equivalent) who are accountable for correct classification and for ensuring coverage of their domain’s authoritative data sets. Data Owners approve domain-level classification standards, endorse remediation priorities, and attest annually to completeness and accuracy (see GRC-ATTEST-2026-04-15, submitted 2026-04-17T10:42:03Z). Data Stewards, designated by Data Owners, operationalize the policy within their domains, maintain catalog entries, coordinate issue remediation, and validate that metadata reflects current classification status. Data Custodians in Technology are responsible for platform-level enablement of classification metadata, ensuring that authoritative tagging is reflected consistently across integrated repositories and lineage artifacts. Control Partners, including Information Risk & Compliance (IRC), Privacy Office, Records Management, and Internal Audit, provide challenge, independent monitoring, and periodic assessments against policy requirements.

This division of responsibilities is documented in the Data Governance Responsibility Matrix (Ref. DCG-RACI-2026 v2.1), which is maintained by the Enterprise Data Governance Office (EDGO). The matrix is authoritative for audit purposes and is reviewed semi-annually to reflect organizational or system changes. Changes to role assignments are tracked via ServiceNow request items and require approvals from the originating business line, EDGO, and IRC (e.g., SNOW-RITM-00418267, approved 2026-05-29T16:58:44Z).

2.3 Operating Rhythm, Artifacts, and Documentation
The policy lifecycle is governed by the Document Management Standard and retained in the Corporate Policy Repository under identifier POL-DATA-CLASS-25.1. The annual review cycle includes a formal impact analysis, stakeholder consultation, and Executive Sponsor approval. The most recent review (Policy Review Ticket EDGO-GOV-4187) commenced 2026-03-01T09:00:00Z and closed 2026-04-12T13:21:15Z, confirming no material changes required and extending the effective period to 2027-04-30. Supporting artifacts include:
- Data Classification Assessment Worksheet (DCG-AW-2026 v1.4)
- Data Domain Inventory Register (DDIR-2026 v5.0)
- Records Retention Mapping Crosswalk (RMS-XW-2026 v3.3)
- Governance Metrics Pack (GM-Pack-Q2FY26)

All artifacts are version-controlled and referenced in meeting minutes. The EDGO maintains a unified backlog in the Governance Portfolio (JIRA project key: EDGO-GOV) to manage policy enhancements, classification disputes, and domain onboarding activities. Tickets carry standardized metadata for severity, impacted domain, and cross-functional reviewers. As of 2026-06-30, the backlog reported 63 open items, with a median age of 12.6 days and on-time closure of 91.3% against the 10-business-day service objective (Ref. GM-Pack-Q2FY26, tab “Backlog Performance”).

2.4 Decision-Making and Escalation
Classification disputes that cannot be resolved at the domain level are escalated to the DQSG for adjudication. The DQSG applies the criteria set forth in Section 3 and records rationale in the Classification Decision Log with supporting evidence from the catalog and domain documentation. Decisions requiring a change to a domain-standard classification pattern are presented to the EDGC for ratification. Example: DEC-2026-109 (Retail Structured Products – Client Reporting Extract), initiated 2026-05-08T14:23:17Z, was resolved at DQSG with EDGC ratification on 2026-05-27T11:05:02Z, and implemented via catalog update MDA-CHG-002913. Escalation timelines are standardized: domain review (up to 5 business days), DQSG review (up to 10 business days), and EDGC ratification (next scheduled meeting or extraordinary session as needed). Issue closure requires evidence of catalog update, steward confirmation, and, when relevant, Records Management crosswalk adjustment.

2.5 Training, Communication, and Attestation
Training on the Data Classification and Governance Policy is mandatory for Data Owners, Data Stewards, and Data Custodians. The required modules are LH-DCG-101 (Foundations of Data Classification) and LH-DCG-201 (Stewardship and Catalog Maintenance). Completion is tracked in Meridian Learning Hub and reconciled quarterly with EDGO records. As of 2026-06-15, completion rates were: Owners 98%, Stewards 96%, Custodians 95% (Ref. EDU-REP-2026Q2). Role-based attestations are captured in the Meridian GRC Portal; control partners review variances and follow up with remedial action plans documented in EDGO-GOV tickets. Communications regarding policy updates are disseminated via the Governance Bulletin (GB-2026-07) and posted to the Data Governance SharePoint hub with links to current artifacts and FAQs.

Section 3. Data Classification Framework

3.1 Overview and Objectives
The Meridian Capital Data Classification Framework establishes a consistent, risk-based method for categorizing information assets to enable proportionate governance, quality management, and records handling across business processes and technology platforms. The framework is intended to be pragmatic and business-aligned, reflecting the materiality of potential impacts to clients, markets, operations, and the firm’s reputation. It is applicable to structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data and is implemented through authoritative metadata in the enterprise catalog.

3.2 Classification Levels and Criteria
Meridian Capital adopts four classification levels that are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive for enterprise-managed data:
- Public: Information approved for general release without restriction, including published financial reports, marketing collateral post-approval, and publicly accessible product information. Public data requires standard governance oversight to maintain accuracy and brand consistency.
- Internal: Business information intended for use within Meridian Capital, where unauthorized external disclosure would be undesirable but not expected to cause material harm. Examples include process documentation, internal performance dashboards, and routine operational reports. Internal data is shared on a need-aligned basis within the firm.
- Confidential: Sensitive business information where unauthorized disclosure, alteration, or misuse could have tangible adverse effects, including regulatory scrutiny, contractual non-compliance, or client relationship impact. Typical examples include nonpublic client information, transactional data sets not designated as market-facing, and management reporting supporting decision-making.
- Restricted: Highly sensitive information where unauthorized access or misuse could result in significant regulatory, financial, or reputational consequences. Examples include select categories of personally identifiable information processed under strict legal obligations, board-level deliberative materials, and data subject to heightened regulatory handling terms.

Classification is based on potential impact across four dimensions: client trust, regulatory considerations, financial exposure, and contractual commitments. The assessment considers the highest reasonably foreseeable adverse outcome across these dimensions; the most conservative applicable level prevails. Where data sets combine elements of differing sensitivity, the aggregate classification aligns to the most sensitive component unless the data is demonstrably segregable in practice and in governance.

3.3 Assessment Approach and Documentation
Data Stewards conduct initial and periodic classification assessments using the Data Classification Assessment Worksheet (DCG-AW-2026 v1.4). The worksheet captures the business purpose, data elements, consuming processes, geographic considerations, and contractual constraints. Evidence supporting the assigned level, including links to authoritative sources, is recorded in the Meridian Data Atlas (MDA) catalog entry. Data Owners review and approve the assessment; approval history is preserved within the catalog’s governance workflow. Any changes to classification status are logged with rationale and timestamped approvals (e.g., MDA-HIST-CL-004782, updated 2026-06-21T09:17:04Z).

3.4 Labeling, Metadata, and Catalog Integration
Classification labels are represented as standardized metadata attributes within the enterprise catalog and propagated through authorized lineage views. Labels must be applied at the lowest practical granularity that the steward can maintain reliably (e.g., dataset, table, file collection) and must be consistent with domain-level classification standards. The catalog entry includes: classification level, assessment date, next review date, Data Owner and Steward identifiers, and references to applicable records retention schedules. The Records Retention Mapping Crosswalk (RMS-XW-2026 v3.3) links classification levels to retention categories, ensuring that records management practices remain aligned with the data’s defined sensitivity and business purpose.

3.5 Reassessment Triggers and Review Cadence
Classification decisions are reviewed at least annually and more frequently upon material changes to business context, data composition, or usage patterns. Triggers include mergers and acquisitions, entry into new markets, onboarding of significant consumers, or material contract changes. For example, RCL-REV-2026-031 (Wealth Advisory Client Insights Mart), initiated 2026-05-30T08:52:19Z and closed 2026-06-21T09:17:04Z, advanced the dataset from Internal to Confidential following expansion of analytics attributes approved by the Data Owner. The review cadence for Restricted datasets is semi-annual, with interim confirmation required for high-visibility processes as directed by the EDGC.

3.6 Cross-Border and Residency Considerations
Where data residency requirements apply, Data Stewards coordinate with the Privacy Office and Records Management to confirm that classification decisions appropriately reflect jurisdictional obligations and contractual terms. The Cross-Border Data Working Note (CBD-WN-2026-02) provides a reference checklist for residency determination and documentation. Any jurisdictional overlays that affect data handling expectations are recorded in the catalog with links to governing agreements or notices, ensuring transparency for downstream consumers and auditability for control partners. Residency annotations do not alter the base classification level but may impose additional governance steps which are tracked in the catalog as compliance attributes.

3.7 Metrics, Coverage, and Continuous Improvement
The effectiveness of the classification framework is measured through enterprise metrics maintained by EDGO and reviewed by the EDGC. As of Q2 FY26, classification coverage across cataloged assets measured 92.4% against a 95.0% target, with 18 of 20 priority domains above threshold and two domains (Corporate Functions Analytics and Third-Party Data Feeds) on remediation plans (EDGO-GOV-4312 and EDGO-GOV-4325). Median time to initial classification for new assets was 9 business days from catalog onboarding, within the 10-day service objective. Automated recommendations within the catalog platform provided 68% suggestion accuracy at the level designation, with 21% requiring steward adjustment and 11% escalated for multi-stakeholder review (Ref. GM-Pack-Q2FY26, sections “Coverage” and “Recommendation Quality”). Trend analysis indicates steady improvement in both coverage and cycle time following deployment of the standardized worksheet and enhanced steward training completed in May 2026.

Continuous improvement is driven by retrospectives conducted quarterly with Data Stewards, captured in Lessons Learned Log LL-DCG-2026-Q2. Action items from these sessions inform incremental updates to guidance materials and steward enablement sessions. The EDGC reviews a subset of reclassification decisions each quarter to validate consistency of application across domains and to ensure that the framework remains aligned to evolving business needs and external obligations. Any proposed framework refinements are documented in EDGO-GOV tickets, undergo consultation with control partners, and, upon approval, are reflected in the next policy review cycle to maintain currency and clarity for all stakeholders.

Page 5 — Data Classification and Governance Policy — Meridian Capital
Document ID: MRC-DG-001 | Version: 1.7 | Effective Date: 2026-04-01 | Data Governance Office (DGO)

Section 3. Roles, Accountability, and Decision Rights
Meridian Capital’s data governance operating model is grounded in clear assignment of authority and accountability across business and technology domains. Ownership of business meaning and usage rests with the first line of defense, while control design and challenge are performed by independent functions. Decision rights are defined to minimize ambiguity, promote timely execution, and ensure that classification outcomes are consistently applied across data domains. This structure is codified in DGO Charter Ref. DGO-CH-2026-02 and reviewed annually by the Data Governance Council (DGC).

3.1 Data Owners (First Line)
A Data Owner is the accountable executive for classification, usage approval, and lifecycle outcomes for a defined data domain (e.g., Client, Trade, Market, Finance). Data Owners are appointed by the relevant Business Head and recorded in the Data Authority Register (DAR) under record keys DAR-CLNT-01 through DAR-FIN-07, maintained by the DGO. Responsibilities include endorsing initial classification decisions, approving material classification changes triggered by new use cases, and attesting to compliance with metadata and retention requirements. Data Owners ensure that domain-aligned processes incorporate classification labels at origination and that business teams understand permissible dissemination. Quarterly, Data Owners provide written attestations (see Attestation Batch ATST-Q2-2026, 2026-06-28T17:00Z) confirming that domain datasets are accurately classified in the enterprise catalog and that any remediation items are captured in the service management queue. Ownership changes must be recorded within five business days in the DAR; reference ticket SNOW-REQ-673829 shows the most recent transfer for the Corporate Actions dataset.

3.2 Data Stewards (First Line)
Data Stewards act on behalf of the Data Owner to operationalize classification outcomes and maintain data context. They curate business metadata, coordinate with Technology to embed labels in pipelines, and monitor data quality indicators relevant to classification (e.g., presence of personal identifiers, trading strategy text). Stewards maintain stewardship backlogs in Jira (e.g., DGSR-2026-1045, DGSR-2026-1093) and partner with the Metadata Operations Team to complete catalog enrichment. Stewards also prepare materials for DGC meetings, including lineage visuals and mapping of controls to classification levels, ensuring transparency and audit readiness. Performance of stewardship obligations is tracked through the Stewardship Compliance Score (SCS), a composite metric derived from on-time attestation, catalog completeness, and timely closure of remediation tasks.

3.3 Data Custodians (Technology)
Data Custodians, primarily within Corporate Technology Operations (CTO) and the Data Platforms & Integration (DPI) team, are responsible for implementing and sustaining classification labels at the system and integration layers. While Custodians do not set business classification, they are accountable for ensuring that labels, tags, and metadata attributes persist through data movement and that catalog synchronization jobs complete within defined SLAs. Custodians manage service queues related to tagging failures, catalog ingestion defects, and schema drift that may affect classification fidelity (e.g., SNOW-INC-884216 opened 2026-05-17T09:42Z and resolved 2026-05-18T13:06Z by DPI). Custodial work is monitored via weekly operational reviews chaired by the CTO Data Services Manager, with outcomes recorded in the DataOps Review Log (DORL-2026-WK21).

3.4 Control Partners (Second Line and Independent Functions)
The Information Risk & Control (IRC) function serves as second line for classification governance, conducting thematic reviews and challenging first line decisions against regulatory obligations and enterprise risk appetite definitions. IRC maintains the Classification Control Library (CCL), which maps classification levels to required control themes (e.g., access governance, vendor oversight, retention). Legal & Compliance provides interpretive guidance on regulatory data categories while Internal Audit independently assesses the effectiveness of the classification framework through periodic audits (latest audit ref: IA-24-DC-003, fieldwork concluded 2026-05-10). Findings and management action plans are logged in the Enterprise Issue Management (EIM) tool with cross-links to relevant datasets and owners; EIM-DC-2026-014 tracks remediation concerning completeness of lineage for certain market data feeds.

3.5 Governance Forums and Review Cadence
The Data Governance Council (DGC) is the senior decision-making forum for classification standards and escalations. It convenes monthly, chaired by the Chief Data Officer (CDO). Agendas include review of classification metrics, material change requests, and thematic risk findings. Minutes are recorded under DGC-MIN-YYYYMM-DD; for example, DGC-MIN-202606-21 documents the approval of the 2026 metadata minimums and endorsement of the quarterly classification attestation results. Supporting forums include:
- Domain Working Groups (DWGs): Monthly sessions focused on domain-specific classification implementation, chaired by Data Owners or delegates. Recent DWG-TRADE-2026-06 addressed harmonization of portfolio strategy descriptors.
- Technology Enablement Review (TER): Biweekly CTO-led meeting to ensure platform alignment and to track deprecation/upgrade impacts on labeling persistence; see TER-2026-12 for catalog connector rollout status.
- IRC Challenge Clinics: Quarterly reviews targeting consistency of interpretation across high-impact datasets; session logs (IRC-CC-2026-Q2) reflect guidance on cross-border data handling alignment with classification levels.

3.6 Documentation and Evidence Management
All classification artifacts are maintained in the enterprise data catalog and linked collaboration repositories. The canonical inventory resides in the Catalog of Record (CoR), with dataset GUIDs serving as the unifying keys (e.g., GUID-CLNT-4231A, GUID-MKT-7720C). Evidence supporting classification decisions, including lineage extracts, data profiling summaries, legal memos, and DGC approvals, is retained in the DGO-controlled SharePoint workspace (Site ID: SP-DGO-1462) and mirrored to the Records Management archive per retention schedules. Versioned documents carry the applicable dataset GUID, version date stamp (UTC), and approver UPN; sample: CLNT-4231A_CLASS_DECISION_v2026-06-20T15:30Z_approved@meridiancap.com. ServiceNow and Jira tickets referenced in these artifacts must include the dataset GUID and classification level in their metadata fields to support traceability and audit queries. The DGO performs monthly completeness checks against these linkages; the 2026-06 check (DGO-QC-2026-06, completed 2026-06-29T18:12Z) reported 98.4% link coverage and opened five remediation tasks for missing lineage attachments.

3.7 Decision Rights Clarification
Decision rights are delineated to avoid duplication and to expedite resolution. Data Owners approve initial classification and material reclassifications; Data Stewards recommend and execute routine catalog updates; Custodians implement enabling controls; IRC issues formal challenges where necessary; DGC makes binding determinations on contested matters. In case files where urgency requires interim designation pending DGC review, the Data Owner’s endorsement serves as the temporary authority and must be recorded with a time-bounded validity in the CoR metadata. The DGO tracks all interim designations and ensures their conversion to final status following the next DGC meeting. As evidenced in case DGCR-2026-045, the interim classification for an analytics dataset was ratified within two weeks, reflecting adherence to the defined governance cycle.

Section 4. Classification Levels and Criteria
Meridian Capital applies a four-tier classification model designed to support regulatory compliance, client obligations, and prudent risk management. Classification is determined by business context, legal constraints, contractual commitments, and potential impact from unintended disclosure or misuse. Each level is defined by sensitivity, required control themes, and distribution posture. Determinations are recorded in the enterprise catalog and supported by documented rationale and evidence, as described in Section 3.6.

4.1 Level Definitions
- Public: Data intended for unrestricted dissemination, including content published on meridiancap.com, corporate press releases, and regulatory filings once formally submitted and publicly available. Although broadly accessible, such data remains subject to accuracy, records, and branding standards. Catalog entries for Public data reference communications approvals (e.g., MKT-APR-2026-031) to affirm release status.

- Internal: Business information suitable for use by Meridian Capital personnel and approved contractors under standard confidentiality agreements. Examples include internal policies, non-client-specific operational reporting, and training materials. Internal data requires baseline governance controls with no external distribution absent authorized channels. The catalog denotes Internal with the tag CLASS=INTERNAL and links to the owner’s attestation.

- Confidential: Data that, if improperly disclosed, could cause client, regulatory, or commercial impact. Representative examples include client account attributes, transaction details, pricing arrangements, proprietary models, and operational metrics containing limited identifiers. Confidential data is subject to enhanced governance with specific oversight on sharing, vendor usage, and data residency. The catalog entry will include a completed impact rationale, legal reference, and Data Owner approval (e.g., CLNT-4231A_CLASS_DECISION_v2026-06-20T15:30Z).

- Restricted: Data of heightened sensitivity whose exposure could result in significant regulatory, financial, or reputational harm. This level encompasses sensitive personal information, strategic deal documentation, pre-public financials, and select trading or risk parameters. Restricted datasets are governed with the most stringent control themes, heightened monitoring, and strict distribution restrictions. Restricted designation requires explicit DGC ratification noted in council minutes and catalog status flags (e.g., DGC-MIN-202606-21; dataset GUID-RSK-9812F).

4.2 Classification Criteria and Rationale
Classification determinations consider: the presence and granularity of personal data; contractual obligations with clients and counterparties; regulatory categorizations under applicable jurisdictions; market sensitivity of the content; aggregation levels; and the business context of intended use. The DGO maintains a reference compendium mapping common data elements to indicative levels, updated semiannually based on regulatory guidance and audit feedback. While this compendium aids consistency, final classification reflects the composite of factors captured in the decision record and validated by the Data Owner. For instance, aggregated metrics lacking identifiers may be Confidential due to business sensitivity even where no personal data is present. Conversely, certain identifiers may necessitate Restricted handling when combined with specific contextual fields. All decisions cite source references (Legal memos, control library entries) and include a review horizon date.

4.3 Labeling and Catalog Tagging Standards
All datasets registered in the Catalog of Record must carry a single primary classification level and may include secondary sensitivity qualifiers (e.g., TIME-CRITICAL, CLIENT-SPECIFIC) to enhance downstream handling rules. Labels are applied using controlled vocabulary values maintained by the Metadata Operations Team (Metadata Dictionary Ref. MDD-2026-05). Each dataset record must also populate the following minimum metadata: Business Owner UPN, Steward UPN, Domain, Data Element Summary, Regulatory Relevance Indicator, Residency Indicator, Retention Category Reference, and Lineage Summary. Tagging must be consistently propagated to views, extracts, and scheduled outputs; Custodian teams ensure synchronization jobs complete within established SLAs, with exceptions logged for remediation (SNOW-TASK-902714 closed 2026-06-22T11:08Z after successful tag repair on a finance reporting extract). Label presentation in user-facing catalogs reflects definitive values; deprecated labels, if any, remain searchable but are flagged with end dates and mapped successors to preserve historical traceability.

4.4 Metrics, Monitoring, and Attestation
The DGO monitors classification health through key indicators published in the monthly Data Governance Scorecard. As of the 2026-06 cycle (DGS-2026-06, published 2026-06-30T14:00Z):
- Catalog Coverage: 96.7% of in-scope datasets carry a current primary classification (target ≥ 95.0%). Coverage improved 1.2pp month-over-month following completion of DWG remediation tasks DGSR-2026-1045 and DGSR-2026-1088.
- Attestation Timeliness: 94.3% of Data Owner attestations submitted by the due date (target ≥ 95.0%); three domains submitted within the grace window and have action plans to meet the next cycle timelines.
- Accuracy Validation: 98.1% of sampled classifications aligned with IRC validation outcomes (target ≥ 97.0%). Two variances were identified in market analytics outputs and are tracked in EIM-DC-2026-016 with expected closure 2026-08-15.
- Tag Propagation Health: 99.2% of lineage hops retained classification tags during scheduled synchronization tests (target ≥ 99.0%). One transient defect (SNOW-INC-889302) was resolved without downstream distribution.

Quarterly, the DGO performs thematic reviews focusing on high-impact domains and cross-border datasets. The Q2 review (DGO-THM-2026-Q2) sampled 45 datasets designated Restricted and confirmed that rationale statements adequately cited regulatory considerations and contractual clauses where applicable. The DGC endorsed the findings and requested a focused review of vendor-hosted datasets in Q3 to validate consistency of catalog labels with third-party inventories.

4.5 Cross-Border, Third-Party, and Records Alignment
Classification outcomes must align with cross-border data handling considerations documented by Legal & Compliance. Data with jurisdictional restrictions includes catalog attributes indicating permitted processing and storage locations, along with the authoritative reference. For third-party engagements, Vendor Management and IRC review the vendor data inventory to confirm that classification labels are recognized and that contractual documents reflect appropriate data handling posture. The Third-Party Data Review log (TPDR-2026-06) records confirmations for six vendors onboarding analytics datasets; two vendors required updates to inventory mappings prior to go-live (TPDR-ACT-2026-06-04). Records Management ensures that classification is harmonized with retention schedules; datasets carry a Retention Category Reference linking to the Records Schedule Identifier (e.g., RS-CLNT-12, RS-TRD-07). Annual alignment checks verify that Restricted and Confidential datasets have explicit retention determinations and that destruction or archival criteria are documented at the dataset level in the catalog.

4.6 Continuous Improvement
Classification is periodically recalibrated to reflect changes in regulatory environment, business models, and data usage patterns. The Semiannual Standards Review (SSR) process, logged under SSR-2026-H1, evaluates emerging data types, updates the indicative mapping compendium, and recommends refinements to metadata minimums. Approved changes are recorded in DGC minutes and scheduled for rollout via the Technology Enablement Review cadence. Completion is tracked through ServiceNow change tasks and evidenced in the catalog change log, ensuring traceability from policy intent to operational implementation. The 2026-H1 SSR introduced clarifications on analytical feature stores and re-affirmed primary label precedence when multiple qualifiers are present, with full adoption confirmed by 2026-06-30T23:00Z in the DGS-2026-06 audit trail.

Section 5. Data Inventory and Catalog Maintenance

5.1 Enterprise Data Catalog Scope and Content

Meridian Capital maintains a centralized Enterprise Data Catalog (EDC) as the authoritative register of structured and semi-structured data assets in scope of this Policy (Ref: MCGP-DC-001 v2.3, Section 2). The EDC enumerates datasets produced, consumed, or curated by enterprise platforms, including but not limited to analytic warehouses, operational data stores, reporting marts, regulatory submission repositories, and approved third-party data feeds. For each registered dataset, the catalog record includes, at minimum: business title; system of record or source; business purpose aligned to an approved use case taxonomy; classification label as defined in Section 3; dataset owner and data steward with directory identifiers; data domain and sub-domain; critical data element (CDE) indicators; retention category per Records and Information Management (RIM) schedule; distribution profile (internal, inter-affiliate, vendor); last certified date; lineage summary; and data quality scoring metadata.

The Data Governance Office (DGO) is accountable for EDC standards, schema, and change control, while Data Platform Operations (DPO) ensures catalog service availability, access provisioning, and integration with pipeline registration mechanisms. Data Domain Stewards within each business-aligned data council are responsible for the accuracy and completeness of descriptive metadata and for timely attestation activities. The EDC is deemed a Tier 1 control repository for purposes of operational risk and audit evidence collection.

5.2 Dataset Registration and Onboarding

All new datasets that are persistently stored, repeatedly produced, or broadly consumed by more than one functional area must be registered in the EDC prior to first production availability. Registration encompasses population of required metadata fields, assignment of classification labels consistent with Section 3.2, confirmation of data ownership (business and technical), declaration of CDEs, and linkage to applicable data quality rules. DPO facilitates registration through the enterprise intake workflow, while the requesting squad must designate an accountable business owner and steward prior to approval. The EDC does not accept records without identified custodians, and records without classification labels are auto-flagged for remediation.

During the onboarding phase, DGO verifies that glossary terms referenced in the submission correspond to approved definitions in the Enterprise Business Glossary (EBG). Where new terms are proposed, the DGO coordinates review with the Enterprise Data Stewardship Council (EDSC). The lineage summary entered at onboarding must reflect the logical flow from source domain to target domain with system-of-record markers. Physical lineage artifacts may be attached as evidence where applicable, but the catalog record itself remains descriptive and technology-agnostic.

5.3 Periodic Recertification and Attestations

All active EDC records undergo periodic recertification to sustain policy alignment and metadata currency. Recertification cadence is defined as quarterly for datasets labeled Confidential and biannually for datasets labeled Internal. Public datasets may follow an annual cadence unless otherwise mandated by regulatory commitments. Recertification requires the dataset owner and steward to jointly attest to the validity of classification labels, owner/steward assignments, data domain mapping, CDE flags, retention category, and lineage summary. Where changes are identified, a standard change request must be logged to update the EDC and, as needed, downstream metadata repositories.

The DGO coordinates attestation waves and issues campaign notifications via enterprise workflow tooling. Each attestation captures the attestor’s name, role, timestamp (UTC), and disposition. Campaign evidence is retained for not less than five years in alignment with the Corporate Audit Evidence Standard. Illustrative completion log entries for the Q2 cycle include: MC-GOV-ATT-2026-Q2-0197 (2026-06-14T09:42:18Z, Global Markets Data Steward, certified), MC-GOV-ATT-2026-Q2-0241 (2026-06-15T16:05:51Z, Retail Banking Data Owner, update required), and MC-GOV-ATT-2026-Q2-0303 (2026-06-20T12:21:07Z, Risk Analytics Data Steward, certified). Items flagged “update required” trigger follow-up tickets for metadata correction and, if relevant, reclassification reviews.

5.4 Metrics and Reporting

The EDC is monitored through a defined set of key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational metrics reported to the Data Governance Steering Committee (DGSC) monthly. Core KPIs include: catalog coverage (registered datasets as a percentage of eligible datasets), timely registration (percentage of datasets registered prior to production availability), attestation completion rate by due date, stale record rate (records with last certified date older than policy threshold), lineage completeness (presence of upstream/downstream references and system-of-record markers), and CDE completeness (percentage of declared CDEs with linked quality rules). As of the 2026-06 reporting cycle (Report Ref: DGSC-2026-06-EDC), catalog coverage measured 96.8% against a target of 98.0%, timely registration measured 92.4% against a target of 95.0%, and stale record rate measured 3.1% against a threshold of ≤2.0%.

Operational metrics are reviewed at the DGO weekly stand-up. The 2026-06-21 session (Meeting ID: DGO-WSU-2026-25, 08:30–09:00 UTC) documented 57 open remediation items associated with stale records, with 41 assigned to Retail & Wealth domains and 16 to Corporate Lending. Average age of open remediation items was 18.6 business days. Ticket references included SNOW: MC-SNOW-GOV-24317 (stale record remediation, Corporate Treasury), SNOW: MC-SNOW-GOV-24402 (owner re-assignment, Wealth Data Mart), and JIRA: DGOV-1278 (lineage enrichment, Merchant Acquiring). DGO noted an improving trend in lineage completeness following targeted stewardship workshops conducted during May (Training Log: DGO-TRN-2026-05-GL-02).

Internal Audit (IA) completed a limited-scope review of EDC controls on 2026-05-29 (Audit Ref: IA-DATA-2026-07). Observations included: (1) inconsistent use of standardized business purpose descriptors in 14 of 120 sampled records; (2) missing CDE indicators in 6 of 120 sampled records within the Corporate Lending domain; and (3) delayed recertification completion in two steward groups past the quarterly deadline. All observations were rated low to moderate significance and were addressed through a corrective action plan coordinated by DGO and domain stewards.

Remediation actions were logged under CAP Plan ID: DGO-CAP-2026-EDC-01 with target dates between 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-30. Section 6. Metadata and Lineage Standards

6.1 Minimum Metadata Standard

Meridian Capital requires a consistent baseline of metadata for all cataloged datasets to support discoverability, risk management, and regulatory reporting. The minimum standard includes: (a) descriptive metadata (title, description aligned to the EBG, business owner, steward); (b) structural metadata (schema name, entity count, update frequency as a controlled vocabulary, and data domain classification); (c) classification metadata (policy label per Section 3.2 and any relevant regulatory designations); (d) quality metadata (CDE indicators, linked quality rules with measurement frequency and rule owners, and last measurement outcome); and (e) lineage metadata (source/consumer summaries, system-of-record identification, and transformation context at a logical level). Each field must be populated using approved controlled vocabularies where available to promote semantic consistency and reduce reconciliation overhead across domains.

The EBG serves as the canonical glossary for business terms and CDE definitions. The DGO curates the EBG with input from domain councils and publishes monthly updates (Release Notes: EBG-RN-2026-06, EBG-RN-2026-07). Dataset records must reference EBG terms rather than freeform descriptions wherever a term exists. Where a new or revised term is necessary, stewards initiate a glossary change request referencing the associated dataset tickets and proposed definitions. The EDSC adjudicates glossary changes within the standard service target of 15 business days and documents decisions, rationales, and version increments.

6.2 Lineage Capture and Verification

Lineage is captured at two complementary levels to balance accuracy with operational practicality: logical lineage (data domains, sources, and consumer pathways described in business terms) and standardized transformation context (e.g., join, aggregate, derive indicated at a categorical level). The intent is to provide traceability sufficient to support impact analysis, regulatory inquiries, and quality incident triage without overburdening product teams with unnecessary technical detail. For designated regulatory reporting datasets, lineage must additionally identify the chain of accountability by role (owner, steward, and control reviewer) to support attestations required by the Regulatory Reporting Controls Framework.

Verification of lineage accuracy is performed during onboarding, during recertification events, and in response to material changes in upstream sources or downstream consumption. The DGO conducts sampling-based spot checks monthly, selecting a minimum of 5% of datasets in each domain or five datasets, whichever is greater. The 2026-06 lineage verification memo (Memo: DGO-LIN-VER-2026-06) reported 94.1% conformance to standard, with remediation tasks raised for missing consumer references (JIRA: DGOV-1317, DGOV-1321) and ambiguous source descriptors (JIRA: DGOV-1323). All identified gaps were assigned to domain stewards with a 20 business day target completion and tracked through the governance dashboard.

6.3 Data Quality Governance

Data quality (DQ) governance is integrated with metadata and lineage to ensure critical elements are understood, monitored, and improved. CDEs must have defined quality rules with clear dimensions (accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, uniqueness) and measurement cadences, along with an accountable rule owner. Rule definitions are stored in the Quality Rule Library and linked to the EDC entries for traceability. Quality measurement outcomes are summarized as a rolling 90-day score for each dataset, displayed in the EDC to promote transparency and facilitate prioritization.

DQ incidents are logged through the enterprise issue management process when measurement outcomes breach predefined operating thresholds. During 2026-Q2, 23 DQ incidents were raised across four domains (Incident Range: DQ-INC-2026-044 to DQ-INC-2026-066). The majority (61%) pertained to completeness deviations in onboarding attributes for small business lending, traced to delayed upstream enrichment. Remediation closed within the target window for 20 of 23 incidents; three incidents required extended monitoring through July (Extensions: DQ-INC-2026-059-E1, DQ-INC-2026-061-E1, DQ-INC-2026-064-E1). The Risk & Compliance Analytics (RCA) team reviewed corrective actions and confirmed that residual risk remained within appetite as documented in the Q2 Data Risk Report (RCA-DRR-2026-Q2).

6.4 Classification Change Management

Classification labels are subject to change based on evolving content, usage context, or regulatory guidance. Changes to dataset classification must follow the standardized governance workflow to ensure proper review, impact assessment, and communication. Requests are initiated by the business owner or steward via the governance ticketing queue with rationale linked to evidence (e.g., updated use case approval, modification of data fields). DGO performs an initial sufficiency check and routes the request to the relevant domain council for endorsement. Where cross-domain impacts are identified, the DGSC adjudicates final disposition.

Illustrative tickets from the 2026-Q2 cycle include: MC-GOV-CLF-2026-072 (Retail Deposits Reporting Mart; requested change from Internal to Confidential due to enrichment with sensitive customer attributes; approved 2026-05-18T11:07:44Z), MC-GOV-CLF-2026-083 (Market Data Snapshot; requested change from Confidential to Internal following removal of proprietary vendor attributes; conditionally approved pending vendor contract alignment, resolved 2026-06-10T15:53:29Z), and MC-GOV-CLF-2026-091 (SME Risk Scoring Features; no change; rationale insufficient). All determinations are recorded in the Classification Decision Log with references to the EDC record IDs and attendant notifications to subscribing consumers.

6.5 Audit Readiness and Evidence Retention

To maintain audit readiness, Meridian Capital preserves metadata change records, attestation outcomes, lineage verification memos, and DQ incident closeout summaries as formal evidence. Evidence retention aligns with the Corporate Audit Evidence Standard and the RIM schedule, with a minimum retention of five years for governance artifacts. Evidence must be retrievable by dataset, domain, and reporting period within reasonable timeframes as defined by the Audit Service Level Charter.

Internal and external assurance activities are supported through a standing evidence package that includes: the latest EDC extract for in-scope datasets; attestation campaign reports; lineage verification sampling results and remediation tracking; quality rule inventories and 90-day score summaries; and a listing of classification changes over the prior 12 months with decision rationales. The 2026-07-08 evidence package prepared for IA (Package ID: IA-REQ-2026-07-EDG) met all completeness and timeliness criteria, with IA acknowledgment recorded at 2026-07-10T10:18:02Z. Where clarifications are requested, the DGO coordinates consolidated responses across DPO, domain stewards, and RCA to ensure consistent messaging and traceability.

6.6 Performance and Risk Metrics

The DGSC monitors a consolidated dashboard of governance performance and risk indicators. As of the July 2026 cycle (Dashboard Ref: DGSC-DB-2026-07), the following were recorded: (a) EDC catalog coverage at 97.3% (trend improving), (b) lineage completeness at 93.8% (flat), (c) attestation on-time rate at 95.6% (above target), (d) average DQ incident time-to-close at 8.4 business days (target ≤10), and (e) classification change average cycle time at 12.2 business days (target ≤15). The stale record rate within Wealth was identified as an emerging watch item at 2.6% (threshold ≤2.0%), with a corrective plan underway (CAP: DGO-CAP-2026-EDC-02).

The DGSC directed the DGO to present a Q3 plan emphasizing glossary adoption consistency, targeted steward enablement for complex lineage scenarios, and closer integration of DQ outcomes into quarterly business reviews. These actions are logged in the Governance Roadmap (Roadmap ID: DGO-RMP-2026-H2) with milestones, accountable owners, and reporting checkpoints to sustain momentum and reinforce policy adherence across business lines.

6. Data Stewardship and Ownership Model

Meridian Capital’s data stewardship and ownership model establishes accountable roles for the lifecycle governance of data assets across business lines and platforms. The model distinguishes between the Data Owner (business executive accountable for use, quality, and compliance within a defined domain), the Data Steward (operational role responsible for day-to-day governance actions and coordination), the System Custodian (technology role overseeing the hosting platform and operational integrity of data systems), and the Data User (employees and contractors consuming data in accordance with permitted purposes). Role charters are maintained by the Data Governance Office (DGO) and are version-controlled under repository GOV-CHAR-REG-01, with the current approved version 3.2 ratified by the Data Governance Council (DGC) on 2026-05-28 at 10:00 ET, recorded in meeting minutes DGC-MM-2026-05.

Data Owners are appointed by the relevant Business Unit Executive in consultation with Information Risk Management (IRM) and Legal & Compliance (L&C), ensuring alignment between regulatory accountabilities and operational oversight. Each appointment defines a scope statement, including in-scope systems-of-record, reference data sets, and derived data pipelines. Data Stewards are nominated by the Data Owner and confirmed by the DGO following verification of competency criteria, training completion, and conflict-of-interest checks. System Custodians are designated by Enterprise Architecture & Platforms (EAP) and documented through configuration records in CMDB reference CMDB-CI-DATA-ALL, with cross-references to the stewardship registry. All assignments and changes are recorded through ServiceNow change tickets (e.g., SNOW-CHG-0041927 closed 2026-06-11 16:42 ET by EAP/Platform Operations) to maintain auditability of role coverage.

6.1 Stewardship Appointment and Tenure

Stewardship appointments are for a standard 24-month term with mid-term confirmation at 12 months. Nominations are initiated via the Data Stewardship Register request type in the DGO service catalog (reference DGO-SC-REG), linked to a JIRA workflow for approvals (e.g., GOV-JIRA-1462 approved 2026-06-03 09:18 ET by DGO Governance Lead). Appointees must maintain an active Meridian training profile, remain within the policy-defined organizational unit, and not simultaneously hold roles that could create conflicting accountabilities (e.g., internal audit assignment within the same data domain). The DGO produces a quarterly coverage report, evidencing that 100% of Tier 1 domains had designated Data Owners and 98.6% had designated Stewards as of 2026-06-30 (2 open items tracked under DGO-TRACK-2026-287 and DGO-TRACK-2026-293, both with remediation plans due Q3).

6.2 Onboarding and Continuing Education

All Data Owners and Stewards must complete the Data Classification Foundations module and the Data Governance Responsibilities module within 90 days of appointment. Continuing education is required annually and is refreshed to reflect changes in regulatory expectations, emerging operational practices, and lessons from assurance activities. Training completions are recorded in the Learning Management System (LMS) under learning path DGO-LP-CLASS-01, with evidence synchronized daily to the stewardship registry. As of 2026-06-30 21:00 ET, automated LMS feed DGO-TRN-FEED-2026-06 reported 97.2% on-time completion for newly appointed Stewards (n=107), with four in grace period statuses and two escalations to Business Unit leadership (ref. ESC-DGO-2026-015 and ESC-DGO-2026-016). The DGO monitors training quality through post-course assessment analytics; the trailing-quarter mean assessment score was 88.4%, with targeted content updates scheduled under SNOW-CHG-0042311 to improve clarity around borderline classification scenarios.

6.3 Delegations and Coverage

Temporary delegations are permitted for planned absences or workload peaks, provided there is continuity of governance decisions and documentation quality. Delegations are time-boxed, must be approved by the Data Owner (for Steward delegations) or the DGC Secretariat (for Owner delegations), and are documented via delegation records (DLG-REG-YYYY-SEQ) with explicit start and end dates. As of 2026-06-15, there were 23 active delegations (median duration 14 days) with no coverage gaps detected by the DGO automated assurance script MC-DGO-ASSURE-17, evidenced by the 2026-06 monthly compliance pack DGO-COMP-2026-06. Coverage metrics are presented to the DGC in the monthly dashboard, which also highlights upcoming delegation expiries to prompt renewal or reversion notifications.

7. Classification Review Cadence and Evidence Collection

The classification review cadence is designed to uphold currency and consistency of classifications across systems, records, and derived data. All Tier 1 data domains must undergo a comprehensive classification attestation annually, while Tier 2 and Tier 3 domains follow an 18-month and 24-month cadence respectively. Independent of cadence, material change triggers (e.g., new data elements introduced to systems-of-record, change in business use, third-party onboarding, or regulatory developments) initiate interim reviews to confirm that classifications remain appropriate. Reviews are recorded in the Governance Review Register (GRR) with unique identifiers (e.g., GRR-2026-0817 for the Treasury Liquidity Data review completed 2026-06-07 15:26 ET).

7.1 Review Triggers and Coordination

Material change triggers are sourced through three input channels: technology change control notifications from EAP, new product approval outputs from the Product Governance Committee, and external developments from L&C. For example, CRQ-EDP-2026-2198 (deployment of a schema expansion within the Enterprise Data Platform) triggered GRR-2026-0799 on 2026-05-30, resulting in a limited-scope attestation within 10 business days and a no-change conclusion for pre-existing classifications. Similarly, LEG-ALERT-2026-044 (interpretive guidance update issued 2026-06-12 08:03 ET) prompted an out-of-cycle review in Wealth Advisory Data (GRR-2026-0824), with revised narrative justifications added to the classification rationale repository.

7.2 Evidence and Artefact Standards

Each review must produce a complete artefact set comprising: the updated Data Inventory extract aligned to the corporate metadata standard (GOV-META-STD v5.1), the signed classification attestation by the Data Owner, a rationale statement referencing data elements and business use, and, where relevant, linkage to third-party data handling clauses maintained by L&C. Evidence is stored in the centralized repository GOV-EVID-CLASS with cross-links to the metadata application of record. Artefact completeness is validated by the DGO within five business days of submission; any gaps are logged as documentation findings (e.g., DGO-FND-2026-0312 closed 2026-06-19 12:47 ET following receipt of a corrected rationale statement from Corporate Lending).

7.3 Sampling and Quality Review

To ensure classifications are applied consistently at the data element level, the DGO applies a risk-weighted sampling methodology calibrated each quarter in consultation with IRM. For the period ending 2026-06-30, the sample size was set at a minimum of 10% of elements for Tier 1 domains, subject to a floor of 50 elements per domain, with increased sampling for domains with prior documentation findings. The Q2 aggregate concurrence rate between Steward-applied classification and independent DGO review was 96.8%, with 3.2% requiring minor narrative enhancement and 0.4% logged as misclassification requiring correction (two items within Capital Markets Reference Data, both remediated under GOV-JIRA-1499 by 2026-06-28). No issues were escalated beyond routine remediation thresholds, and the DGC noted steady improvement over the preceding three quarters.

7.4 Scheduling and Backlog Management

The DGO maintains a rolling six-month review calendar published to all stakeholders on the first business day of each month. Where resource constraints or competing priorities arise, scheduling adjustments are managed through the Review Planning Forum with Business Unit and EAP representation. As of the 2026-06 cycle, there were three reschedules within the same quarter (refs. GRR-RS-2026-020 through -022), each supported by documented rationale and alternate dates within the published window. The backlog stood at zero at quarter-end, with no impact on the annual coverage objectives.
