8. Metrics, Key Risk Indicators, and Reporting

Meridian Capital monitors a defined set of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) to evidence operational effectiveness of data classification and broader data governance. KPI measures focus on execution (e.g., review timeliness, training completion, stewardship coverage), while KRIs focus on exposure (e.g., volume of unclassified assets, overdue reviews, and discrepancies across systems). Metrics are compiled monthly by the DGO Analytics team and validated by IRM prior to distribution. The Executive Data Governance Dashboard (EDGD) is issued on the fifth business day (e.g., EDGD-2026-06 published 2026-07-08 09:00 ET) and reviewed at the Data Governance Council meeting within the same month.

For the period ending 2026-06-30, KPI performance was as follows: classification review on-time completion rate of 98.3% against a target of ≥97%; stewardship role coverage of 99.2% for Tier 1 domains against a target of 100%; training on-time completion of 97.2% for newly appointed Stewards and 95.6% annual refresh across all incumbents against a target of ≥95%. KRI readings included 0.6% of cataloged data sets flagged as “classification pending” (target ≤1.0%), 1.1% of reviews in “approaching due” status (within 30 days of due date), and 0.3% discrepancy rate between the metadata application of record and downstream consumption layers as detected by reconciliation controls. All outliers were within management appetite set by the DGC (ref. DGC-APP-2026-01).

8.1 Metadata Quality and Fitness

Sustained governance depends on reliable metadata. The DGO’s Metadata Quality Program evaluates completeness, consistency, and validity of critical fields, including data element name, business definition, classification label, authoritative source, and Data Owner assignment. In Q2 2026, field completeness across Tier 1 domains averaged 99.1% (prior quarter 98.7%), with two domains targeted for improvement initiatives due to definitional ambiguities identified in IRM’s spot checks (IRM-RSK-2026-0054 and IRM-RSK-2026-0059). Duplicative entries in the catalog decreased to 0.4% following cleansing activity executed by EAP under change ticket SNOW-CHG-0042059, resulting in a notable decline in classification inquiry tickets (EDP-SR-2026-11412 and -11437) related to catalog confusion. The DGO has scheduled a data definition harmonization workshop series for Q3 (DGO-WS-2026-03) to further reduce definitional variance and enhance reuse.

8.2 Reporting Cadence and Governance Forums

Reporting is structured to enable oversight at appropriate levels. Monthly operational reports (DGO-OPS-M-YYYYMM) are distributed to Data Owners and Stewards, highlighting upcoming review obligations, training status, open findings, and near-term risks. Quarterly business reviews (QBRs) with each Business Unit summarize performance trends and discuss remediation progress, culminating in a consolidated enterprise view for the Executive Risk Committee (ERC). On 2026-07-15 11:30 ET, the ERC reviewed Q2 outcomes (ERC-MM-2026-Q2), noting positive trendlines in review timeliness and a minor uptick in documentation findings concentrated in one domain, for which a targeted quality intervention plan was endorsed (plan reference DGO-QI-2026-07).

9. Issue Management and Remediation Tracking

Governance issues are identified through scheduled reviews, ad hoc observations, data catalog monitoring, and independent assurance. All issues are logged in the Governance Issue Register (GIR) and categorized by severity, thematic area, and business domain. Standard statuses include Open, In Progress, Ready for Validation, and Closed, with each issue assigned a Remediation Owner and an IRM Validator. Service level targets are applied to ensure timely resolution commensurate with issue materiality and complexity. The GIR is reconciled weekly with the JIRA board (GOV-JIRA) to confirm status integrity and linkage to remediation work items.

During Q2 2026, 48 issues were raised and 52 were closed (including 10 from the prior quarter). The median time-to-close was 24 calendar days, with 95th percentile at 41 days, within the management target. Illustrative examples include: GOV-JIRA-1481 (ambiguity in classification rationale wording for a payment reference field) opened 2026-06-06 10:12 ET by DGO and closed 2026-06-21 16:03 ET after revised rationale approval by the Data Owner; GOV-JIRA-1493 (inconsistent application of “Internal” vs. “Public” on marketing collateral metadata) opened 2026-06-17 09:45 ET by Corporate Marketing and closed 2026-06-30 14:26 ET following catalog update and communication by L&C. No issues met the criteria for management escalation beyond the DGC in the reporting period.

9.1 Thematic Findings and Root Causes

Thematic analysis performed by DGO Analytics (report DGO-TH-2026-Q2) identified three recurring themes: documentation precision in rationale statements, timeliness of catalog updates following minor schema changes, and occasional divergence in classification labels between upstream and downstream views where propagation routines awaited scheduled runs. Root cause categorization indicated process timing (46%), documentation clarity (38%), and tooling integration constraints (16%). Targeted actions include refining the rationale template (GOV-TPL-CLASS-RAT v2.1 issued 2026-07-01), aligning release windows between EAP and catalog synchronization jobs (CRQ-EDP-2026-2307 scheduled for Q3), and reinforcing Steward coaching through the continuing education module refresh.

9.2 Remediation Governance and Validation

Remediation plans are documented with clear deliverables, acceptance criteria, and target dates. The DGO monitors progress through weekly checkpoints with Remediation Owners, and IRM performs validation upon completion to confirm risk reduction and sustainability. Validation requires demonstration that the underlying cause has been addressed and that control operation is evidenced over a defined observation window. In Q2, 100% of closed issues included IRM validation evidence stored alongside the resolution artefacts in the GIR repository, with two items additionally sampled by Internal Audit as part of its rolling review (see Section 9.3).

9.3 Independent Assurance and Continuous Improvement

Internal Audit completed an advisory review (IA-2026-07) of the data classification operating model during May–June 2026, focusing on role clarity, evidence sufficiency, and metric reliability. The review concluded that the control design remains appropriate and operating effectively, with three low-priority observations regarding documentation standardization and metric lineage traceability. Management actions (DGO-ACT-2026-071 through -073) were agreed with target dates in Q3 and are tracked within the GIR. The DGC reviewed the advisory report on 2026-07-10 13:00 ET and endorsed management’s responses. Additionally, IRM’s periodic oversight (IRM-OVS-2026-06) found no instances where classification decisions deviated from policy definitions and noted improved collaboration between Data Stewards and EAP in pre-implementing classification impact assessments for planned data model changes.

The DGO continues to mature the control environment through incremental enhancements grounded in observed performance and assurance feedback. Planned initiatives for Q3 include enhancing the metadata lineage narrative to improve interpretability by non-technical stakeholders, refining dashboard thresholds to sharpen KRI sensitivity without increasing noise, and further developing stewardship communities of practice to share domain-level insights. These measures are aligned with the DGC’s 2026 maturity roadmap and will be reported in subsequent cycles with measurable targets and evidence of effectiveness.

Section 7: Monitoring and Stewardship Operations

7.1 Data Classification Review Cadence
Meridian Capital maintains a structured cadence for classification verification to ensure that data assets remain appropriately labeled throughout their lifecycle. The Data Governance Office (DGO), in partnership with the Enterprise Data Stewardship Team (EDST), executes a rolling, quarterly review of classification attributes across prioritized domains, with specific focus on systems of record and high-velocity integration points. For Q2 FY2026, the cadence was aligned to the operational calendar as follows: Core Banking (Weeks 2–3), Capital Markets (Weeks 4–5), Corporate Functions (Weeks 6–7), and Enterprise Shared Services (Weeks 8–9). Each review cycle encompasses automated attribute reconciliation against the authoritative classification taxonomy (Policy Annex A) and targeted manual sampling at a rate of 2% of records for domains with high data volatility and 0.5% for low-volatility domains. Findings and remediations are recorded centrally under Governance Change Requests (GCR) in the DGO tracker with approval gates anchored to control DCP-07.02.

The Q2 FY2026 review logged 147 GCRs (ref. DGO-GCR-2026-0421 through DGO-GCR-2026-0567) between 2026-04-08T09:15Z and 2026-06-12T16:40Z. Of these, 83% were resolved within the target SLA of 15 business days, with an average resolution time of 9.6 business days, as documented in ServiceNow records (Task Group: GOV-STEWARDSHIP, Queue Owner: EDST-NorthAmerica). Recurrent themes included harmonization of legacy labels on decommissioned archive objects in the Lakehouse Zone-2 store and correction of default “Internal” labels on vendor onboarding extracts that should have been “Confidential” per the vendor data specification mapping. Materiality assessments concluded no downstream reporting impacts; the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) liaison confirmed residual risk as low following remediation validation on 2026-06-18T11:22Z (ERM Note: ERM-VAL-2026-219).

7.2 Stewardship Work Intake and Ticketing
All data classification and governance changes, exceptions, and clarifications are routed through the standardized work intake in the DGO-managed queue. The intake form enforces mandatory metadata capture (data domain, system, steward, proposed classification state, rationale, lineage segment, and effective date), anchored to form version DGO-FRM-CL-3.6. The EDST triages tickets daily at 13:00 local time with representatives from Lines of Business (LOB) present on alternating Wednesdays. Tickets with potential cross-domain impact trigger an automatic consultation with the Integration Architecture Team (IAT) to assess interface metadata propagation. During the April–June 2026 window, 312 intake tickets were raised (INTK-2026-1001 through INTK-2026-1312), with 289 progressing to actioned status and 23 closed as informational. The proportion of tickets originating from automated drift detection alerts increased to 41%, reflecting stronger signal generation from the metadata observability platform (Release v2.4.1 deployed 2026-05-03T02:10Z under change CHG-2026-3119).

Steward assignments continue to be benchmarked against the RACI defined in Section 3, with each record showing accountable business stewards and technical stewards. Variance analysis from the EDST monthly dashboard (published 2026-06-28T08:00Z) indicated that 96% of tickets had the correct steward of record, and 4% required reassignment due to changes in LOB ownership following the Treasury Operations reorganization (Ref. HR-ANN-2026-045). All reassignments were closed within the same reporting period, and stewardship continuity was maintained via temporary coverage protocols approved by the Data Governance Council (DGC) on 2026-06-14T14:22Z (DGC Minutes Item 7b).

7.3 Evidence of Control Operation
Evidence management for classification controls remains centralized in the Governance Evidence Repository (GER), tagged under folder taxonomy GER/Policy-DCP/Section-7. Artifacts include automated control run logs, steward sign-offs, validation samples, and remediation attestations. For the period ending 2026-06-30, 51 evidence bundles were uploaded and cryptographically timestamped by the Records Management Team (RMT), with index references GER-EVD-2026-0701 through GER-EVD-2026-0751. Spot checks by Compliance Assurance (CA) on 2026-06-21T10:05Z verified traceability from policy clause to control, and from control to execution evidence, for a random sample of five bundles. The CA memo (CA-Q2-2026-19) recorded “adequate” sufficiency and recommended a standardized summary sheet for each bundle to streamline external auditor walkthroughs planned for November 2026. The DGO has accepted this recommendation, with the template pilot scheduled for the July control cycle under task DGO-IMPR-2026-009.

To preserve consistency, evidence retention and retrieval follow the enterprise retention schedule (Information Schedule IS-RET-5.1) and are cataloged with immutable identifiers. Retrieval tests executed on 2026-06-25T12:44Z by the Internal Audit Liaison verified sub-5 minute retrieval for all tested items. No anomalies were noted, and the retrieval drill was logged in the quarterly control attestation (Q2 FY2026, Attestation ID: DCP-ATT-2026-Q2-07) endorsed by the Chief Data Officer (CDO) on 2026-06-30T17:30Z.

7.4 Data Lineage Verification Routine
Lineage verification ensures that classification attributes are accurately propagated across ingestion, transformation, and publishing layers. The Metadata Engineering Team (MET) maintains reference lineage models for Tier-1 and Tier-2 systems, updated under configuration baseline MET-BSL-2026-06. During the Q2 campaign, MET completed 24 lineage walkthroughs across data products with critical reporting obligations, reconciling observed metadata flows with declared patterns. Three minor discrepancies were identified within the Capital Markets analytics pipeline where derived fields inherited “Internal” instead of “Confidential” due to missing attribute joins in a transformation view. Corrective tasks (MET-FIX-2026-118 to MET-FIX-2026-120) were implemented by 2026-06-10T15:55Z, and subsequent verification confirmed accurate propagation with no downstream distribution beyond the internal test sandbox.

Findings were presented to the DGC on 2026-06-14, with action items to expand sampling to Tier-3 systems with high dependency counts. The DGO will augment the sampling algorithm to incorporate dependency centrality metrics from the enterprise catalog, targeting a 10% uplift in lineage coverage for Q3 FY2026. Progress against this objective will be reported via the Governance Operations Scorecard, ensuring transparent oversight and timely course corrections should KPI drift be observed.

Section 8: Metrics, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement

8.1 Key Performance and Risk Indicators
The DGO maintains a balanced set of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) to quantify the health of classification and governance activities. The Q2 FY2026 KPI suite comprises: timely closure of classification tickets (target ≥ 90% within SLA), evidence bundle completeness (target 100% of in-scope controls), steward coverage (target ≥ 98% of critical data elements with assigned stewards), and lineage verification breadth (target ≥ 85% of Tier-1/2 assets reviewed within cycle). KRIs evaluated in the same period include percentage of unlabeled data objects discovered by automated scans (threshold ≤ 0.5%), variance between declared and observed classification at distribution boundaries (threshold ≤ 1.0%), and repeat remediation occurrences within 60 days (threshold ≤ 2 incidents per domain).

For the reporting period ending 2026-06-30, Meridian Capital achieved 92.4% on-time closure for classification tickets, 100% evidence completeness, 98.7% steward coverage, and 86.1% lineage verification breadth. KRIs remained within tolerance: unlabeled discovery rate at 0.34%, boundary variance at 0.62%, and repeat remediation at 1 incident in Corporate Functions (HR Analytics dataset, ref. DGO-GCR-2026-0519 follow-up DGO-GCR-2026-0554). The KRI watchlist documented no red thresholds; however, the DGO flagged a yellow trend in lineage breadth owing to scope growth in the Capital Markets domain. A targeted intervention plan (DGO-IMPR-2026-012) allocates additional MET capacity during July–August to sustain breadth above target as new data products are onboarded.

8.2 Quarterly Reporting and Council Oversight
The Governance Operations Scorecard is issued within five business days of quarter-end and disseminated to the DGC, ERM, Compliance Assurance, and LOB data offices. The Q2 FY2026 scorecard (Report ID: DGO-RPT-2026-Q2-07, distributed 2026-07-05T09:00Z) includes trend analyses over a rolling four-quarter window, variance narratives for any indicator exceeding ±5% of target, and curated appendices with ticket-level anonymized exemplars. The DGC convened on 2026-07-10T13:00Z (Meeting ID: DGC-2026-07) to review results, with the Chair noting sustained performance in evidence management and improvements in steward coverage following the Treasury Operations realignment. The Council assigned two follow-up tasks: assess classification change lead time within Capital Markets new product launches (Owner: EDST-CapitalMarkets; Due: 2026-08-15) and develop a proposal for incorporating third-party data trust scores into KRIs (Owner: ERM-ThirdPartyRisk; Due: 2026-09-05).

Meeting minutes recorded consensus that current tolerances remain appropriate for the enterprise risk appetite and regulatory commitments. The Council also ratified the Q3 FY2026 monitoring plan, including expanded sampling in Tier-3 systems and an interim deep-dive on cross-border data transfers affecting classification at jurisdictional boundaries. Action tracking for these decisions is centralized under DGO-ACT-2026-0701 through DGO-ACT-2026-0706, visible to all stakeholder teams via the governance portal.

8.3 Training, Communication, and Awareness Metrics
Meridian Capital’s training model emphasizes stewardship competency and consistent application of classification principles. During Q2 FY2026, the Learning & Development (L&D) function, in coordination with the DGO, delivered three targeted modules: Fundamentals of Data Classification (LMS Course: DCP-101), Stewardship Responsibilities (DCP-201), and Metadata Quality Essentials (DCP-205). Completion metrics as of 2026-06-29T18:00Z show 99% completion for DCP-101 across in-scope roles (2,146 of 2,165 assigned learners), 96% for DCP-201 among designated stewards (487 of 507), and 94% for DCP-205 within technical roles (catalog curators and MET engineers). Post-course assessments indicate a median score of 92%, with course feedback highlighting the effectiveness of case-based scenarios tied to recent governance tickets (e.g., INTK-2026-1234 and INTK-2026-1279).

The DGO complemented formal training with monthly communications, including “Governance in Practice” briefs featuring anonymized examples of correct classification decisions and common pitfalls. The May brief (DGO-COM-2026-05) focused on supplier data onboarding alignment and achieved a 72% open rate within the steward community. These materials, archived under GER/Communications, serve as reinforcement and evidence for cultural adoption, supporting audit narratives of sustained governance maturity.

8.4 Audit Readiness and Evidence Coordination
In anticipation of the annual external audit scheduled for November 2026, the DGO and Internal Audit (IA) have instituted an audit readiness workstream with defined milestones. A pre-assessment walkthrough was conducted on 2026-06-22T14:30Z (Session Ref: IA-PRE-2026-06), covering the design and operation of DCP controls mapped to Sections 6–9 of this policy. IA’s field memo (IA-MEMO-2026-18) concluded that control design remains robust and implementation evidence is sufficiently comprehensive. Two enhancement opportunities were recorded: consolidating lineage verification summaries into a single quarterly annex and standardizing cross-references between ticket IDs and evidence bundles. The DGO has initiated tasks DGO-IMPR-2026-013 and DGO-IMPR-2026-014 to address these opportunities ahead of the Q3 close.

Evidence coordination protocols require that each control assertion be linked to a minimum of one representative ticket, one validation sample, and one attestation, each bearing immutable identifiers and timestamps. The Records Management Team has confirmed capacity to respond to auditor document requests within three business days based on Q2 drill performance. All coordinating artifacts will be versioned and placed under change control per Records SOP RM-CTRL-4.2, with IA granted read access to the GER audit workspace by 2026-08-01.

8.5 Tools, System of Record, and Data Catalog Alignment
The enterprise metadata catalog remains the system of record for classification attributes, steward assignments, and lineage references. During Q2 FY2026, the MET deployed incremental enhancements to catalog synchronization to reduce latency in attribute updates, with observed mean propagation time improving from 2.4 hours to 1.1 hours post-release (CHG-2026-3119). The DGO validated these improvements through synthetic change events logged under test tickets TST-DGO-2026-022 through TST-DGO-2026-026 between 2026-05-06T10:00Z and 2026-05-07T16:30Z. No discrepancies were noted between catalog state and downstream reporting layers in the validation window.

Exceptions to catalog primacy are not permitted under this policy and are monitored via the automated drift detection alerts integrated into the stewardship intake. Remaining variances were attributable to deprecation of non-active data products awaiting archival confirmation. These items are tracked under DGO-GCR-2026-0561 through DGO-GCR-2026-0567 with an expected closure by 2026-07-25.

Continuous improvement remains a core tenet of Meridian Capital’s governance practice. The DGO will maintain a transparent improvements backlog, link each improvement to empirical KPI/KRI observations, and report progress at each DGC session. 7.4 Data Retention and Disposition Controls
Meridian Capital applies standardized, defensible retention and disposition controls to all classified data assets, aligning with jurisdictional regulatory requirements and internal business needs. Retention periods for each classification category and record series are defined in the Enterprise Records Schedule (ERS v12.4) and bound to the Authoritative Systems of Record (ASoR) and their downstream consuming platforms through metadata-based controls. The Records & Information Management (RIM) function, in partnership with the Data Governance Office (DGO) and Enterprise Data Management (EDM), performs quarterly validation of control adherence, with attestation logged under RR-Attest identifiers (e.g., RR-Attest-2026Q2-017) and cross-referenced to platform evidence repositories. As of 2026-06-30, ASoR-to-ERS binding coverage was 96.8% across the Confidential and Restricted classifications, with remediation in-flight for residual legacy repositories (ServiceNow PRB-009871; owner: Data Platform Engineering, opened 2026-05-14T10:42Z).

Disposition events are initiated only upon automated confirmation that no legal hold, regulatory moratorium, or active investigation is present. Legal hold statuses are reconciled weekly against the Litigation Response Team (LRT) registry (LRT-REG-2026.2) and recorded in the RIM ledger with immutable event IDs (e.g., DISP-EVT-26-004512). System-generated disposition manifests list record series, volume, classification label, and disposition rationale code. The Control Monitoring Team (CMT) conducts monthly spot checks of 10% of closed manifests to confirm traceability from business justification to ERS mapping and disposition authorization (audit trail references: CMT-SC-26-06-221 through -229). Exceptions were not identified in the last two review cycles; one advisory note was logged concerning descriptive accuracy of a rationale code (GOV-14271, closed 2026-06-05T15:18Z).

7.4.1 Defensible Disposal Certification
A defensible disposal certification protocol is used to document that end-of-life data is retired in alignment with policy. Upon completion of a disposition batch, the accountable Data Owner and the RIM lead jointly certify compliance, producing a DDC record containing: (i) ERS clause reference; (ii) inventory scope statement; (iii) hold reconciliation reference; (iv) attestation timestamps; and (v) peer review confirmation by EDM. Certifications are assigned sequential identifiers (e.g., DDC-2026-Q2-041) and retained in the Governance Evidence Repository (GER) for a minimum of seven years. Quarterly sampling by Internal Controls Assurance (ICA) confirms the presence and completeness of these certifications; for Q2 2026, 22 of 22 sampled DDCs were present with full metadata (ICA Sample Set: ICA-SMP-26Q2-B).

Where disposal cannot proceed due to external constraints (e.g., statutory extension), RIM documents a deferment record (DEF-REC-26-0079) citing the applicable obligation, expected reassessment date, and the accountable function. Deferments are reviewed in the RIM–Legal operating committee every six weeks; status and trend metrics are summarized in the Governance Steering Deck (DGO-STEER-26Q2, slide 14).

7.4.2 Legal Hold Reconciliation
The Legal function maintains authoritative control over litigation and investigation holds. Data sets tagged as Confidential or Restricted are cross-checked against the Legal Hold Index (LHI-2026.2) using dataset-level persistent identifiers. Weekly reconciliations are executed on Tuesdays 12:00Z, with discrepancy tickets automatically opened in the Governance Queue for review by the Hold Coordination Team (HCT). During the period 2026-05-01 through 2026-06-30, five discrepancies were detected (HOLD-DISC-8821 to -8825), primarily due to deprecated dataset aliases following platform consolidation. Root-cause analysis (RCA-26-044) concluded that the metadata lineage map was not updated following a decommission event (CHG-004771, completed 2026-05-19T21:06Z); corrective action updated lineage references and added a post-change validation checkpoint to the governance change checklist (GOV-CL-12, rev. 7). No premature dispositions were executed; all affected records remained under hold status throughout.

7.5 Data Minimization and Purpose Limitation
Data collection and processing activities are governed by the principles of data minimization and purpose limitation. The Data Intake Review (DIR) process validates proposed data elements against declared business objectives and regulatory bases of processing. Submissions to the DIR include a Purpose Statement, Classification Impact Assessment (CIA form CIA-2026F), and Data Element Inventory with sensitivity designations. The Data Collection Review Board (DCRB) convenes biweekly to assess requests exceeding predefined sensitivity thresholds or seeking new uses for Restricted attributes. Decisions are recorded in DCRB minutes with action items tracked in JIRA (e.g., DCRB-26-143 “Wealth Analytics attribute rationalization,” approved with conditions 2026-06-12T09:30Z).

Minimization performance is measured through the Minimization Ratio (MR), defined as the percentage reduction in proposed attributes retained post-review. For Q2 2026, the enterprise MR averaged 24.1% across all submissions (n=64), with higher reductions in exploratory analytics (31.5%) than in regulatory reporting (8.7%). Purpose statements are version-controlled and time-bounded; where time-limited processing is justified (e.g., pilot programs), a sunset control is recorded with a predefined review date (SUN-CTL-26-028, review due 2026-09-30). The Privacy Office and DGO co-sponsor periodic assessments to confirm that downstream usage remains within the approved scope, evidenced by Data Use Conformance Audits (DUCA-26Q2 series). Nonconformances in Q2 were limited to tagging gaps in derived datasets (DUCA-26Q2-006), remediated through steward-led metadata enrichment (MD-ENR-26-061).

7.6 Quality Assurance and Data Stewardship Metrics
Data quality governance applies standardized dimensions—completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, timeliness, and uniqueness—across classified datasets proportionate to their risk. EDM maintains a central catalog of data quality rules (DQ-RULECAT-2026.2) mapped to data elements, classifications, and control owners. Rule performance is surfaced in the Enterprise Data Quality Dashboard (EDQ-DASH-26Q2), segmented by domain (Client, Product, Finance, Markets) and by classification. For the Confidential class in Q2 2026, median completeness scored 99.2% and validity 98.4%, with two outlier datasets flagged for timeliness degradation linked to upstream batch window compression (DQI-31145 “Trade_Archive_2019 timeliness variance”; DQI-31162 “Collateral_Status feed latency”). Both were tracked to closure with quantitative recovery to threshold in subsequent cycles (EDQ evidence captures EVC-26-1431, EVC-26-1490).

Data Stewards are accountable for rule stewardship, issue triage, and certification of quarterly data health. Steward attestations (ST-ATST-26Q2 series) report rule conformance, open issue aging, and remediation progression. Average open-issue age decreased from 41.3 to 28.7 days quarter-over-quarter, driven by earlier escalation of cross-domain defects to the Data Working Group (DWG) and more consistent root-cause coding (RCA coding accuracy improved to 95.6%). At the same time, Steward Roundtables convened monthly by EDM (minutes MIN-EDM-ST-2026-05, -06) highlighted the need for harmonized domain glossaries to reduce duplicate rule definitions; a unification workstream has been initiated (GOV-14822; target deliverable: GL-UNIF-26Q3-Alpha).

Where quality issues intersect with classification sensitivity—e.g., misapplied labels that impair downstream handling—classification correction tickets are opened in the Governance Queue (CLS-COR-10517) and assigned to the responsible steward with oversight from the DGO. For Q2 2026, nine such corrections were recorded, all resolved within the five-business-day service target, with no downstream policy breaches identified. Continuous improvement activities are documented in the Quarterly Governance Report (QGR-26Q2), accessible to the Data Governance Council and Internal Audit.

8. Oversight Mechanisms and Decision Rights
Meridian Capital’s data governance oversight model is anchored by a tiered committee structure with clearly defined decision rights, accountability, and escalation paths. The model ensures that classification standards, lifecycle controls, and data quality practices are directed by senior leadership and executed consistently across business lines and technology platforms. Charters, quorum requirements, and voting procedures are documented under the Governance Committee Charter Pack (GCCP-2025.3), with annual reviews performed by the Office of the Chief Data Officer (OCDO) and confirmed by the Enterprise Risk Committee.

8.1 Data Governance Council (DGC)
The Data Governance Council serves as the primary decision-making body for enterprise data policy and classification standards. Membership includes the Chief Data Officer (Chair), Chief Information Officer, Chief Privacy Officer, Head of Compliance, and designated Business Data Owners for major domains (Client, Markets, Finance, Risk). The DGC meets monthly on the third Thursday, with formal minutes and action registers retained under MIN-DGC-YYYY-MM-DD identifiers (e.g., MIN-DGC-2026-05-22; quorum achieved 9/11; 62-minute session). In Q2 2026, the DGC ratified the revised Classification Label Definitions (CLD v2.1) and endorsed the Data Steward Competency Model (DSCM-26.1), assigning implementation to EDM with a Q3 target (Action: DGC-ACT-26-052). Voting follows simple majority, with tie-break authority vested in the Chair. Material decisions impacting regulatory posture are also tabled with the Enterprise Risk Committee for awareness (ERC-NOTE-26-018).

8.2 Stewardship Operating Model
The stewardship model assigns Domain Data Owners (DDOs) ultimate accountability for their domain’s data, supported by Data Stewards (DDSs) who manage day-to-day governance execution. Responsibilities are codified in RACI matrices maintained at the domain level (RACI-CLNT-26.2; RACI-MKT-26.1), reviewed semi-annually. DDOs approve classification assignments for new or materially changed datasets, while DDSs ensure metadata completeness, rule stewardship, and policy conformance reporting. Onboarding for new stewards follows a standardized curriculum delivered through the Learning & Development function (L&D), tracked in the LMS under cohort codes (LMS-COH-26-07). The Steward Community of Practice meets bi-monthly to exchange patterns and share domain-specific updates (CoP minutes MIN-CoP-2026-06-07). As of 2026-06-30, coverage was 100% for critical domains, with bench depth increased through deputy assignments in high-volume areas (DWG note DWG-26-044).

8.3 Escalation and Issue Management
A structured, time-bound escalation process ensures that classification and governance issues are triaged and resolved consistently. The Governance Queue in the enterprise ticketing platform categorizes issues as P1 (urgent, regulatory/time-critical), P2 (significant, cross-domain impact), or P3 (localized, informational). Service targets are set at two business days to containment for P1, five for P2, and ten for P3, with progress visibility in the Governance Operations Dashboard (GOV-OPS-DASH-26Q2). Classification disputes are routed to the Classification Review Panel (CRP), a subcommittee of the DGC comprising representatives from DGO, Privacy, and the relevant Business Data Owner. In 2026 Q2, CRP adjudicated 11 disputes (CLS-INC-88214 through 88224), primarily concerning derivative datasets lacking inherited labels. Median time-to-decision was 3.2 business days, with two cases elevated to the DGC for principle-setting due to cross-jurisdictional considerations (ESC-26-019, ESC-26-020). All decisions were documented with rationale and precedence tags to promote consistent future application (CRP-DEC-26Q2 set).

10. Data Quality Governance and Issue Management

Meridian Capital maintains a standardized, enterprise-wide Data Quality (DQ) governance framework to ensure that data assets across all classifications (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) are accurate, complete, timely, and fit for their intended business purpose. The Enterprise Data Governance Office (EDGO), acting as the first line governance function in partnership with Business Unit Data Stewards (BUDS), defines and maintains the DQ standards under Policy Ref: MCDG-POL-001 v3.2 and the associated control library (Control IDs DQ-01 through DQ-11). Oversight and challenge are provided by Information Security Risk (ISR) and the Privacy Office (PO), with Internal Audit (IA) executing periodic audits against these controls. The DQ control objectives are operationalized via Data Platform Operations (DPO) using approved tooling and are monitored through monthly scorecards delivered to the Data Governance Council (DGC).

The DQ framework requires that critical data elements (CDEs) identified through data lineage mapping and regulatory reporting dependencies be registered in the enterprise data catalog with explicit quality rules, accepted thresholds, and assigned ownership. Minimum rule sets are defined per classification tier and data domain (e.g., client, product, transaction, reference). As of 2026-06-30, the catalog contains 7,842 CDEs with 35,109 associated active DQ rules, of which 91.4% have documented business acceptance criteria and remediation playbooks. EDGO maintains a standardized rule taxonomy (accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, validity, uniqueness) and a root-cause taxonomy (source capture, transformation logic, reference data, process handoff, vendor file variance, user input) to enable consistent analysis and reporting.

A cross-functional Data Quality Working Group (DQWG) convenes on the second Tuesday of each month at 15:00 ET, chaired by EDGO with participation from DPO, BUDS, ISR, and L&C. Meeting minutes and decisions are recorded under meeting series DQWG-2026 and filed in the governance repository with timestamp and attendance. At each session, the DQWG reviews: (a) monthly exceptions against thresholds; (b) trend analysis for recurring defects; (c) in-flight remediation plans; and (d) emerging risks identified through change activity (e.g., new data sources, schema changes, vendor onboarding). A standard escalation protocol (DGC-08.4) directs issues that exceed business tolerance, impact regulatory reporting, or persist beyond two remediation cycles to the DGC for executive decisioning.

All DQ incidents are tracked in the enterprise service management platform under the “DG-QUALITY” queue with required metadata fields (CDE ID, system of record, business process, client impact rating, classification tier, rule violated, date first detected, control ID linkage, and data steward). Resolution service levels are defined by severity: Sev1 (regulatory reporting or client detriment risk) MTTR target ≤ 10 business days; Sev2 (material business decisioning impact) MTTR target ≤ 20 business days; Sev3 (localized process impact) MTTR target ≤ 45 business days. Sample incident references during Q2 FY26 include: DG-QUALITY-2026-04177 (opened 2026-04-12T14:33:18Z, Sev2, Transaction Enrichment Completeness; closed 2026-05-03T10:11:04Z), DG-QUALITY-2026-05211 (opened 2026-05-27T09:18:52Z, Sev3, Client Address Validity; closed 2026-06-14T16:44:29Z), and DG-QUALITY-2026-06007 (opened 2026-06-21T12:07:45Z, Sev1, Reference Rate Consistency; remediation ongoing as of 2026-06-30T17:00:00Z under change CHG-PLT-2026-1986).

Remediation plans must specify root cause, interim risk mitigations, target state controls, testing and validation criteria, and communication actions to impacted stakeholders. Closure criteria include: (1) evidence of corrected data or verified compensating controls; (2) production deployment of rule or logic corrections validated by DPO and steward UAT sign-off; (3) 30-day stability window with no regression breaches; and (4) documentation updates in the catalog and runbooks. IA Review ID IA-DG-26-014 confirmed adherence to closure criteria on a sample of 25 closed incidents (April–June 2026), noting one minor documentation gap (missing steward sign-off attachment) remediated via ticket DOC-GOV-2026-00912 on 2026-06-28T08:25:03Z.

To enhance proactive detection, EDGO and DPO implemented stratified sampling and anomaly detection thresholds for high-variance sources. Quarterly recalibration of thresholds is mandated for Restricted and Confidential datasets with materiality ratings High or Critical. Q2 recalibration (Change Advisory CRQ-DATA-2026-1174) reduced false positives for transaction uniqueness rules by 18.6% without degrading sensitivity, as evidenced by back-testing against Q1 breach patterns. The DQWG recorded a 12-month rolling DQ KRI of 0.94 breaches per 1,000 CDE-rule-days for Confidential data, within the DGC-approved tolerance of ≤ 1.10, with a downward trend for three consecutive quarters.

11. Data Lifecycle Governance and Retention Controls

Meridian Capital’s data lifecycle governance encompasses creation, collection, usage, sharing, archival, and disposition, with control objectives aligned to legal, regulatory, and business requirements. Records Management (RM) owns the Master Retention Schedule (MRS) (Document RM-MRS-2026 v5.1), which establishes minimum retention periods by record class and cross-references data classifications and applicable jurisdictions. Lifecycle controls mandate that all new datasets registered after 2025-10-01 include: (a) authoritative system of record designation; (b) retention class mapping to the MRS; (c) destruction eligibility criteria; (d) archival tier selection; and (e) a data owner and steward. Mandatory lifecycle checkpoints are embedded in the SDLC at design sign-off (DLC-01), go-live readiness (DLC-02), and post-implementation review (DLC-03). - DSAR performance (on-time responses involving processors): 99.2%.
- Retention adherence (inbound data): 98.9% sampled compliance; remediation complete.
- Legacy remediation (pre-2025 feeds aligned to EDC): 96.7% complete.

The DGSC assigned a green status to third-party governance with a note to sustain focus on legacy remediation and to deepen vendor-provided metadata integrations. The next cycle will pilot enhanced dashboarding of third-party metrics within the EDC Steward Portal, consolidating VRM confirmations, Privacy SLAs, and RIM retention attestations into a single view (pilot backlog item JIRA-DGO-PORT-2216; target deployment 2026-08-15). All actions remain on track and are monitored through weekly DGO Operations stand-ups (meeting notes DGO-OPS-2026-26 through -28).

Meridian Capital — Data Classification and Governance Policy
Policy ID: MC-DG-001 v3.2
All timestamps are UTC unless otherwise stated.

14. Performance Indicators and Operational Reporting

14.1 Overview and Measurement Approach
The Enterprise Data Governance Office (EDGO), in partnership with Risk & Controls Assurance (RCA) and the Corporate Technology Platform (CTP), maintains a quarterly measurement framework to evidence the ongoing effectiveness of the Data Classification and Governance Policy. Key performance indicators (KPIs) are derived from the control objectives codified in MC-DG-001 v3.2 and from Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) risk taxonomy identifiers RT-DATA-01 through RT-DATA-05. Measurement scope includes all in-scope systems registered in the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) with system criticality ratings C1–C4 and associated data assets recorded in the enterprise data catalog (Atlas v5.19), as of the reference date. KPI computations are generated via the EDGO Metrics Service (EMS) job DGOV-KPI-2026Q2, executed 2026-07-05T02:14:33Z under change record CHG0034879, with peer validation by RCA (validation ticket RCA-VAL-22113).

14.2 KPI Results for Q2 FY2026
For the quarter ended 2026-06-30, catalog coverage achieved 98.6% of in-scope assets (112,384 of 114,015), a 0.4 percentage point improvement over the prior quarter, attributable to onboarding of late-phase CRM microservices (Program REF: CTP-CRM-NextGen) completed under JIRA DGOV-2417 and DGOV-2421. Classification completeness (presence of a current classification label per MC-DG-001 Annex A) reached 99.1% across registered datasets, with 0.9% pending label confirmation at quarter end tied to newly ingested vendor feeds (Procurement Systems Portfolio “Merisource,” platform ID VND-FEED-023). Classification accuracy—measured via stratified sampling against the Data Classification Quality Checklist (RCA-QC-DG-07)—was independently assessed by RCA at 97.8% (95% CI: ±0.6%), reflecting 87 reclassifications logged and closed within SLA (INC0127734 through INC0127816). No systemic mislabeling patterns were identified; remediation actions were tracked to closure with owner attestations captured in ServiceNow tasks SCTASK01988562 and SCTASK01988571.

Data owner attestation for the quarter achieved 99.2% completion (1,842 of 1,857 attestations due), with five attestations deferred to July due to leadership transitions in Institutional Markets Technology (IMT). Deferrals were approved by EDGO under governance case EDGO-ATT-2026Q2-005, with interim custodial sign-off recorded by the Data Stewards Council (DSC) in minutes DSC-Min-2026-06-21. Timeliness of metadata updates met the policy’s 10-business-day standard in 96.5% of cases (target ≥95%), and average update latency improved to 3.2 days from 3.8 days in Q1.

14.3 Control Operating Effectiveness
RCA’s cycle-based testing of controls DG-CL-02 (Classification Assignment), DG-MD-01 (Metadata Completeness), and DG-AU-03 (Governance Review) yielded an aggregate rating of “Effective” for the period, with minor observations recorded in RCA-OBS-2026-0611 and RCA-OBS-2026-0617. Observations pertained to documentation clarity in lineage annotations for cross-domain joins and the need for additional descriptive tags to improve discoverability of Semi-Confidential market reference data. EDGO and Data Architecture Review Board (DARB) jointly agreed on corrective action plans (CAP IDs CAP-DG-0611 and CAP-DG-0617) with target dates 2026-09-15 and 2026-10-01, respectively. Weekly status is surfaced via the DGOV Control Dashboard (Confluence: DGOV/Reporting/Control-Evidence; report snapshot DGOV-RPT-2026Q2-S1 exported 2026-07-06T09:41:02Z).

14.4 SLA Adherence and Operational Throughput
Operational throughput for metadata change tickets averaged 213 tickets/week, with a peak of 267 during the final week of May aligned to quarterly release freeze preparations. SLA adherence for standard classification requests (SLA: 5 business days) was 97.3%, and for expedited requests (SLA: 2 business days, subject to EDGO triage) was 95.8%, influenced by concurrent platform maintenance windows in the lineage engine (reference CHG0035002). Backlog aging over 30 days fell to 1.1% (target ≤2%), aided by cross-staffing from the Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) team for two weeks (Work Order WO-DG-2026-114).

14.5 Governance Forums and Attendance
The Data Governance Committee (DGC) met on 2026-04-11, 2026-05-09, and 2026-06-13 (Calendar series: DGC-2026-Std, Chair: Chief Data Officer). Quorum was achieved in all sessions, and attendance averaged 92% across permanent members (EDGO, RCA, Legal & Compliance (L&C), CTP, ILM, and divisional data officers). Standing agenda items included review of KPI trends, alignment with regulatory commitments (Reg References: 2024-OCIE-Data-03; 2025-ECB-DQ-12), and change approvals for policy-aligned metadata schema extensions (Schema Change Requests SCR-DG-074 and SCR-DG-075, approved with standard controls). Meeting minutes were published within two business days with document links DGC-Min-2026-04, DGC-Min-2026-05, and DGC-Min-2026-06.

14.6 Stakeholder Communications
Quarterly stakeholder communications were issued 2026-07-08T13:27:10Z via the firmwide bulletin (Comms ID: COM-DG-2026Q2) summarizing key outcomes, upcoming attestations, and references to the training refresh cycle due in August. Queries were routed through the EDGO Service Desk queue (ServiceNow Assignment Group: EDGO-SD) with an average first-response time of 2.1 hours and resolution CSAT of 4.7/5 from 312 survey responses (Survey batch SVY-DG-2026Q2-01).

15. Data Quality Alignment with Classification Standards

15.1 Integration of Data Quality Signals
The Data Quality (DQ) Program and EDGO continue to integrate DQ signals with classification metadata to contextualize materiality and remediation priority. During Q2 FY2026, 1,146 DQ rule breaches were recorded across 64 systems; of these, 6.8% intersected datasets labeled Confidential, 41.2% Semi-Confidential, and 52.0% Public/Unrestricted. EDGO applied policy-aligned prioritization to breaches intersecting higher-sensitivity classes, resulting in mean time to remediate (MTTR) of 4.6 days for Confidential data issues versus 6.3 days portfolio-wide. Evidence of prioritization logic is documented in DQ Governance Note DQG-NT-2026-04. RCA independently reviewed prioritization outcomes (RCA-REV-DQ-2026-07) and confirmed alignment.

15.2 Lineage Traceability and Steward Actions
Lineage traceability for high-sensitivity datasets (Confidential and Semi-Confidential) reached 97.2% end-to-end coverage from source to consumption layer (measurement job LIN-COV-2026Q2). Gaps noted (2.8%) pertained to two legacy reporting views in Institutional Lending Analytics (ILA) where source system identifiers were embedded in derived datasets without consistent business term references. DARB assigned remediation actions under JIRA LIN-2651 and LIN-2652, with Data Owners acknowledging responsibility in attestations ATT-DG-ILA-2026-02 and ATT-DG-ILA-2026-03.

15.3 Business Glossary and Term Harmonization
Glossary completeness for required business terms adjacent to classified data reached 95.4% (target ≥95%). The remaining variance is concentrated in regional variations of product taxonomy definitions in EMEA Markets. The Business Glossary Working Group (BGWG) has scheduled harmonization workshops (2026-08-05 and 2026-08-12; Calendar series BGWG-HARM-2026) with proposed term merges captured in Glossary Change Proposals GCP-2026-019 through GCP-2026-024. Impact assessments were logged (IA-DG-2026-EMEA-05) indicating no adverse downstream effects on reporting dimensions.

15.4 Reporting and Independent Review
EDGO issued the Q2 FY2026 Data Quality and Classification Alignment Report (Report ID DGOV-ALGN-2026Q2), approved by DGC on 2026-07-12. RCA completed a sample-based independent review under test plan RCA-TST-DG-2026-02 and concluded that integration of DQ signals into classification-driven prioritization is operating as designed. Follow-up observations emphasize continued training for data stewards on lineage annotation conventions to maintain consistency across systems undergoing cloud migration (Reference Program: CTP-Cloud-Phase3). Training refresh artifacts are filed under TRN-DG-LIN-2026-08.

Meridian Capital — Data Classification and Governance Policy
Policy ID: MC-DG-001 v3.2
All timestamps are UTC unless otherwise stated.

16. Tooling and Automation Governance

16.1 Platform Oversight and Release Hygiene
Tooling supporting the Data Classification and Governance Policy—comprising the enterprise data catalog (Atlas v5.19), the lineage engine (TraceCore v4.7), and the policy evaluation service (Sentinel-DataGov v3.4)—operated within defined service levels during the quarter. Change governance followed Corporate Technology Platform standards with pre-implementation validations recorded under CHG0035002 (TraceCore patch), CHG0035119 (Atlas minor update), and CHG0035228 (Sentinel ruleset refresh). EDGO approved each change after confirming that classification and glossary artifacts passed non-regression checks in the staging environment (Test Cycle IDs: TST-DG-AT-2026-06C, TST-DG-TC-2026-06B). Release notes are archived in Confluence (DGOV/Tooling/Release-Notes) with artifacts attached to JIRA releases REL-DG-2026.06 and REL-DG-2026.07.

16.2 Service Reliability and Monitoring
Service availability for the catalog and lineage platforms was 99.98% and 99.96%, respectively, calculated via monthly uptime reports (OPS-AVAIL-2026-04 through OPS-AVAIL-2026-06). A minor catalog slowness event on 2026-05-18T10:12:55Z (INC0127342) affected query response times for approximately 11 minutes; no data integrity or governance artifacts were impacted. Root cause analysis and capacity adjustments are documented in Problem Record PRB0011889, with final review closed 2026-06-02T15:08:27Z by CTP Operations. Monitoring thresholds for metadata ingestion lag and lineage parse error rates were calibrated during the quarter (Monitoring Change MC-OPS-2026-44), resulting in a 21% reduction in noise-to-signal ratio for alerts addressed by EDGO on-call analysts.

16.3 Automation of Classification Hints
Automated classification hints generated by Sentinel-DataGov v3.4 provided 63.5% pre-population coverage for new datasets, with a human-in-the-loop validation step enforced through EDGO workflow rule WF-DG-VAL-07. Disposition accuracy for hints was measured at 94.1% when reviewed by certified data stewards (certification reference TRN-DG-CS-2025 cohort). Three model drift reviews (MDR-2026-04 through MDR-2026-06) were conducted by the Analytics Controls team to ensure hint performance stability across onboarding of new data domains; all remained within accepted thresholds defined by DGC. Documentation of model features and validation evidence is maintained in the DGOV Model Card repository (Doc IDs MC-SDG-2026-04, MC-SDG-2026-05).

16.4 Integration Interfaces
Interoperability between the catalog, glossary, and lineage platforms is maintained via managed interfaces with schema governance and standard field mappings. During Q2 FY2026, no breaking changes were introduced, and downstream consumers (Reporting Fabric, Data Lake Zones, and self-service portals) received notification summaries (Notice IDs: NTF-DG-2026-0412, NTF-DG-2026-0609) prior to minor field additions. Interface health checks (IFHC-2026Q2) executed on a weekly cadence demonstrated consistent payload validation with a 99.9% pass rate; two transient mismatches were identified and resolved under JIRA INT-DG-581 and INT-DG-589 without impact to policy conformance.

17. Training, Awareness, and Attestation

17.1 Curriculum and Participation
Mandatory annual training “Data Classification Foundations” (TRN-DG-FOUND-2026) and the role-based module “Stewardship in Practice” (TRN-DG-STWD-2026) were delivered to all in-scope personnel. Completion rates as of 2026-06-30 were 98.9% for Foundations (global) and 97.4% for Stewardship (applicable population: 1,146 stewards and custodians). Business unit breakdowns indicate full compliance within Retail Banking Technology (RBT) and minor trailing completion in Corporate Functions Technology (CFT) due to onboarding of new hires in June; targeted catch-up sessions have been scheduled (2026-07-25 and 2026-08-01, session IDs TRN-S-2026-0725A/B).

17.2 Communications and Reinforcement
Awareness campaigns aligned to data classification principles included two firmwide reminders (COM-DG-2026-05R and COM-DG-2026-06R) and a steward community webinar on 2026-06-20 (WEB-DG-2026-06, attendance 312). Feedback surveys (SVY-DG-TRN-2026-02) noted a 4.6/5 satisfaction score with requests for additional examples on lineage annotations and practical glossary authoring tips. EDGO will incorporate this feedback into Q3 updates, with revised microlearning assets tracked under TRN-DG-ML-2026-08.

17.3 Attestation Cycle
Quarterly attestations from Data Owners and Data Stewards affirming classification currency and metadata sufficiency were recorded with 99.2% on-time completion, as noted in Section 14.2. The attestation workflow (ATTEST-Flow v2.1) captured sign-offs, delegation events, and evidence attachments in alignment with records management standards. Independent sample verification by RCA (RCA-VER-ATT-2026Q2) yielded zero discrepancies in the sampled population. Audit trails are immutable and accessible to authorized reviewers per the Role-Based Access framework established by EDGO and L&C.

18. Recordkeeping and Evidence Management

18.1 Evidence Lifecycle
Evidence generated in support of this policy—including KPI extracts, attestation reports, meeting minutes, control test results, and release documentation—is retained according to the Corporate Records Schedule CRS-INFO-07 and tagged with metadata to facilitate retrieval. Q2 FY2026 evidence packages were compiled under Evidence Sets ES-DG-2026Q2-01 through ES-DG-2026Q2-05 with index manifests (Manifest IDs MAN-DG-2026Q2-A/B) and checksum verification logs recorded at the time of archival (LOG-CHKSUM-2026Q2). RCA confirmed completeness and integrity during their quarterly review (RCA-EVID-CK-2026Q2).

18.2 Accessibility and Audit Readiness
Authorized stakeholders may locate current and historical evidence through the EDGO Evidence Index (EEI v1.9), a searchable catalog of document links and metadata references. As part of audit readiness, EDGO executed a mock retrieval exercise on 2026-06-27 (Exercise EX-DG-RETR-2026-02) to confirm two-hour retrieval targets for any evidence class within the prior six quarters; actual retrieval averaged 37 minutes across eight requested artifacts. Evidence pointers and version identifiers were validated against their authoritative sources, and stale pointers identified in the index (n=3) were corrected under ticket EDGO-OPS-2026-092.

18.3 External Assurance Coordination
Where external assurance activities reference classification and governance artifacts, EDGO operates as the single point of coordination, ensuring timely provision of materials and consistency of responses. During Q2 FY2026, requests from two oversight bodies were serviced within agreed timelines (Requests EXT-REQ-2026-11 and EXT-REQ-2026-16), with no follow-up queries outstanding as of 2026-07-15T18:04:09Z. Responses leveraged approved narratives and metrics drawn from DGOV-RPT-2026Q2 and supporting evidence sets.

19. Forward Agenda and Continuous Improvement

19.1 Planned Enhancements
The DGC approved a forward agenda for Q3–Q4 FY2026 focusing on:
- Incremental enrichment of lineage coverage for Semi-Confidential analytical models in Institutional Lending Analytics and Treasury Risk (Program LIN-ENR-2026-H2).
- Expansion of glossary governance to cover regional term harmonization with specific focus on EMEA product taxonomies (BGWG-HARM-2026 execution).
- KPI refinements to segment classification completeness by system criticality and asset lifecycle stage, improving management visibility (KPI-REF-2026-03).
- Training micro-modules targeting lineage annotation patterns and practical metadata examples, addressing survey feedback (TRN-DG-ML-2026-08 rollout).

19.2 Target Metrics and Milestones
Targets for H2 FY2026 are set as follows and were ratified by DGC on 2026-07-12: catalog coverage ≥99.0%; classification completeness ≥99.3%; lineage traceability for Confidential/Semi-Confidential datasets ≥98.0%; attestation on-time completion ≥99.5%; SLA adherence for standard classification requests ≥98.0%. Interim checkpoints are scheduled monthly, with KPI recalculations executed under EMS jobs DGOV-KPI-2026M07 through DGOV-KPI-2026M12. Progress will be reviewed in standing DGC sessions (2026-08-10, 2026-09-14, 2026-10-12) with documented outcomes appended to this policy’s operational annex.

19.3 Dependency and Risk Monitoring
Dependencies include continued platform stability for Atlas, TraceCore, and Sentinel; resource availability within EDGO, RCA, and DARB; and timely data owner participation for attestations and glossary approvals. Risk monitoring will track potential schedule pressure from parallel enterprise programs (e.g., CTP-Cloud-Phase3, CRM-NextGen stabilization) and maintain escalation pathways via the EDGO Portfolio Board (EPB) should KPI trajectories deviate materially from targets. Risk and issue registers are maintained in JIRA (DGOV-RSK-BOARD; issues RSK-DG-2026-014 through RSK-DG-2026-019) with weekly review cadence and cross-functional sign-off.

19.4 Reporting Commitments
EDGO will continue to publish quarterly operational reports within 10 business days of quarter end, with aligned briefing materials for executive sponsors and stakeholders. The Q3 FY2026 report (DGOV-RPT-2026Q3) is scheduled for issuance 2026-10-09, immediately following the close of attestation windows and RCA testing cycles. All metrics and assertions will be backed by traceable evidence and remain consistent with the policy controls defined herein.

End of Pages 23–24.

Meridian Capital
Data Classification and Governance Policy
Page 25 of 25

Section 13: Governance Performance Summary and Forward Agenda
The Data Governance Council (DGC) concluded its FY2026 mid-year review on 2026-06-28T16:45:00-04:00 (Ref: DGC-Minutes-2026-06-28, Meeting ID: DGC-142). The Council affirmed sustained conformance with the approved data classification taxonomy (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and noted incremental improvement in inventory completeness across enterprise repositories. Based on consolidated reporting from Data Governance Operations (DG-OPS), Enterprise Risk & Compliance (ER&C), and the Business Data Stewardship Forum (BDSF), classification coverage reached a validated 96.2% of cataloged assets, an increase of 1.4 percentage points quarter-over-quarter, with residual variance attributable to pending lineage mapping in two product-aligned data domains. The Council directed DG-OPS to continue its targeted remediation backlog execution under Epic DCG-2411 (Jira: DCG-2411), with weekly checkpoint stand-ups and a quantified closure target by 2026-09-30.

Forward agenda priorities were ratified without exception: (1) finalize cross-domain alignment of derivative data element tagging to address propagation fidelity; (2) complete the reconciliation between system-of-record attestations and downstream analytical marts for three high-volume platforms by integrating stewardship attestations into the quarterly business reviews; and (3) standardize regional data handling notices to improve onboarding quality for newly in-scope markets following scheduled platform expansions. The Council confirmed no changes to classification criteria, handling requirements, or record retention parameters in this period. All actions have been recorded in ServiceNow as Task Set TS-DGC-2026-07 (Parent: CHG0036123), with accountability assigned to named steward groups and target states measured via existing Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

Appendix C: Metrics and Reporting Summary (Q2 FY2026 Close)
DG-OPS submitted the consolidated KPI pack (Report ID: DCG-MetricPack-Q2FY26, generated 2026-07-05T09:12:43Z) to ER&C for independent validation. Core measures met or exceeded threshold unless noted as “monitor” status:
- Classification Coverage: 96.2% validated; threshold ≥95.0%; trend positive for three consecutive quarters. Residual 3.8% represents data sets in discovery intake awaiting steward assignment (Intake Queue ID: IQ-2026-217 through IQ-2026-229).
- Tag Fidelity (Propagation Accuracy): 93.7% pass rate in automated lineage checks; threshold ≥93.0%. Monitor status applied for two domains (Credit Risk Analytics, Client Servicing) pending completion of corrective mapping tasks (SNOW PRB0012487, PRB0012491).
- Inventory Completeness: 98.9% for production systems in scope; threshold ≥98.0%. Outliers driven by planned decommission schedules where archival attestations are queued (RetainOps Ticket: RTN-2026-031).
- Stewardship SLA Adherence: 94.8% of classification changes reviewed within 10 business days; threshold ≥94.0%. Noted variance due to concurrent release freezes in June (Change Window: CW-2026-06-14 to CW-2026-06-24, Ref: CHG0035840 coordination).
- Training Completion: 99.3% completion for mandatory annual data handling module among in-scope employees; threshold ≥99.0%. Remaining completions scheduled in July onboarding cohort (HR-L&D Ticket: LND-DC-2026-118).

ER&C’s spot validation (Sample Set: ER&C-SV-2026-06, n=240 assets) produced no material discrepancies. Minor observations (n=7) concerned descriptive metadata consistency (formatting variance in Business Glossary entries). DG-OPS will address via bulk updates under Task DO-2026-444 before next reporting cycle. No audit findings require retrospective reclassification or retroactive control attestations.

Appendix D: Audit Trail References and Evidence Index
All material changes and reviews during this period are traceable through the following authoritative logs:
- Classification Change Approvals: ServiceNow Change Records CHG0035471, CHG0035584, CHG0036123; associated tasks TS-DGC-2026-03 through TS-DGC-2026-07. Each record includes approver IDs, timestamps, and steward comments. Evidence stored in the Governance Evidence Repository (GER) under folder GER/DCG/2026/Q2/CHG.
- Inventory Attestations: Quarterly attestation forms signed by domain stewards (Attestation Batch AB-DCG-Q2FY26) with time-stamped confirmation. Document IDs AB-2026-052 to AB-2026-081; filed in GER/DCG/2026/Q2/ATT.
- Data Quality Cross-Checks: Automated lineage and tag propagation jobs (Job IDs: LIN-AT-2026-0621-A, LIN-AT-2026-0628-B) executed successfully with green status per Operations Control log (OpsCtl-LG-2026-06). Result files archived in GER/DCG/2026/Q2/LIN.
- Training and Awareness: Completion certificates exported from L&D Learning Platform (Export Ref: LND-EXP-DCG-2026-06-30). Verification hash manifest included in the export package metadata for integrity confirmation.

Glossary of Operational Terms (Abbreviated)
- Classification Coverage: Percentage of cataloged data assets with an approved classification status and associated handling tags in the enterprise data catalog.
- Tag Fidelity: Degree to which classification tags are consistently and accurately propagated across lineage from source to derivative assets in integrated systems.
- Stewardship SLA: Target response and review times for designated data stewards to adjudicate classification requests and metadata updates in the workflow queue.
- Inventory Completeness: Alignment ratio between discovered data stores and the official enterprise data inventory, based on approved discovery scans and manual attestations.
- Governance Evidence Repository (GER): Controlled-access repository for storing governance artifacts, including approvals, attestations, and metric exports necessary for internal and external audit review.

Record of Approvals and Sign-Offs
This policy was reviewed and reaffirmed without amendment at the DGC session of 2026-06-28. Formal approvals recorded as follows:
- Chair, Data Governance Council (Role ID: DGC-CHAIR-01): Approval logged 2026-06-28T17:03:19-04:00; ServiceNow Approval ID: APV-003821.
- Head, Enterprise Risk & Compliance (Role ID: ER&C-HEAD-02): Concurrence logged 2026-06-29T09:11:04-04:00; Approval ID: APV-003829.
- Chief Data Officer (Role ID: CDO-01): Final executive acknowledgment logged 2026-06-29T10:22:47-04:00; Approval ID: APV-003834.
- Data Privacy Office Representative (Role ID: DPO-REP-03): Advisory review logged 2026-06-27T15:36:58-04:00; Advisory Note Ref: ADV-2026-114. No conditions attached.

Document Control and Distribution
Document ID: POL-DCG-001; Version: 5.0; Effective Date: 2026-07-01; Review Cycle: Annual (or as directed by DGC). Custodian: Data Governance Operations (DG-OPS). Master copy maintained in the Policy Library (Library Path: PL/DCG/POL-DCG-001/v5.0). This document is distributed to the DGC membership, ER&C, Business Unit Stewards, Enterprise Architecture, Information Lifecycle Management, and the Data Privacy Office. Controlled distribution lists (DL-DCG-Primary, DL-DCG-Stewards, DL-DCG-Executive) are maintained by DG-OPS and reconciled quarterly against HR organizational records. Superseded versions are retired to the Policy Archive with status “Historical – Do Not Use” and immutable retention metadata.

Contact and Escalation Matrix
Routine inquiries and classification workflow support requests should be directed to DG-OPS via the Governance Service Portal (Request Category: Data Classification; Queue: GSV-DGOPS; Reference Prefix: GSV-DC-). For escalations related to policy interpretation, contact the DGC Secretariat (Ticket Prefix: DGC-SCRT) citing the applicable section reference and the affected data domain. Incidents involving suspected mislabeling or handling deviations must be recorded as governance issues in ServiceNow (Issue Type: Governance – Data Classification) and routed to the relevant steward group. Target response times adhere to published SLAs, with priority assignment based on business impact and data classification level. After-hours coverage is coordinated through the Enterprise Operations Center, which will engage the on-call steward according to the monthly rota (Roster ID: DG-OPS-ROTA-2026-07).

Closing Statement
Meridian Capital reaffirms its commitment to proportionate, consistent, and transparent data governance. This policy, supported by robust operational controls, quantified metrics, and documented accountability, remains the authoritative reference for classification and handling across the enterprise. All teams are expected to maintain continuous adherence and to participate in scheduled reviews to ensure ongoing fitness for purpose and alignment with regulatory expectations and business needs.

Executive overview
This report documents the current-state lineage and provenance across priority financial domains for Meridian Capital during Q2 2026. Coverage emphasizes end-to-end traceability of critical data assets supporting statutory and management reporting, with particular focus on Treasury Liquidity, Market Risk, and Regulatory Capital subject areas. The scope includes dataset- and field-level lineage where available, dependency maps for ingestion and transformation layers, and operational evidence of data quality monitoring. The content is designed to support internal attestations (quarterly control confirmations) and to inform continuous improvement tasks already planned for Q3 2026.

Highlights for the period:
- 96.4% lineage completeness across the in-scope subject areas (up from 93.1% in Q1), measured by the proportion of columns with documented upstream origin at least two hops back to source-of-record.
- 100% job-level provenance capture for orchestrated transformations in Finance Analytics workspaces (Airflow and Databricks jobs tagged and linked to business glossary terms).
- Reduction in “unknown source” flags from 41 to 9 through remediation of historical ingestion identifiers and standardization of dataset keys in Bronze and Silver layers.
- No material data control breaches reported; two non-material variances noted and resolved within SLA (details provided on page 2).

- Scope: Treasury Liquidity (DS-TRES-*), Market Risk (DS-MRISK-*), Regulatory Capital (DS-REGCAP-*), and Shared Reference Data (DS-REF-*). Excludes exploratory sandboxes and personal analytic workbooks.

- Provenance controls: run-to-run job identifiers, source snapshot tags, and record counts reconciled against ingestion manifests; non-production environments excluded from metrics.
- Quality indicators: nullness, referential integrity, transformation timeliness, and uniqueness checks, recorded via Data Quality Service (DQS) with daily rollups.

Page 1 — Executive Overview, Scope, and Governance

Document purpose
This handbook establishes Meridian Capital’s standard approach for observing, measuring, and signaling the operational health of ETL pipelines across finance, risk, and enterprise data domains. The content focuses on consistent definitions, shared expectations among support teams, and a traceable record of monitored metrics and alert channels. It is designed to be read alongside the Enterprise Incident Management Standard and the Data Quality Framework Standard. The material reflects routine practices and findings from scheduled reviews and is suitable for general operational reference within the bank.

Parameter set — Document metadata (Ref: DOC-MCE-DP-HBK-ETL-MON-001)
- Title: ETL Pipeline Monitoring and Alerting Handbook
- Business owner: Enterprise Data Engineering (EDE)
- Technical owner: Data Platform SRE (DPSRE)
- Version: 1.2
- Effective date: 2026-07-15
- Classification: Internal Use Only
- Review cadence: Quarterly
- Next scheduled review: 2026-10-10
- Related records: CHG0039482 (Prod dashboard taxonomy update), PRB0012528 (Q1 schedule adherence analysis), KB-ETL-2147 (Metric definitions)
- Distribution list: DPSRE, EDE, Operations Command Center (OCC), Finance Data Stewardship (FDS), Risk Analytics Technology (RAT), Compliance Data Oversight (CDO)

Executive summary
ETL pipelines at Meridian Capital support daily close processes, regulatory reporting aggregates, liquidity projections, credit risk scoring, and departmental analytics. The monitoring estate spans orchestration health, workload performance, schedule adherence, data quality signals, and business-aligned KPIs used by Finance and Risk. The target state emphasizes early detection of degradation, transparent ownership, and consistent alert semantics. This handbook consolidates naming standards for metrics, dashboards and alert identifiers, and the set of reference severity levels used by OCC for daily interpretation.

Scope and applicability
- In-scope workloads: Batch and micro-batch pipelines orchestrated via standard schedulers used by EDE; data movement and transformation jobs landing in governed storage and warehouse targets; data quality controls instrumented through approved libraries.
- Environments: Development (DEV), Quality Assurance (QA), User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and Production (PROD).
- Out-of-scope: Ad hoc analyst notebooks; one-time backfills performed outside standard orchestration; non-data workloads (e.g., web services) except when they serve as upstream dependencies captured in the pipeline inventory.

Parameter set — Environment matrix (Ref: ENV-MCE-DP-ETL-001)
- Orchestration: Apache Airflow (managed), standard DAG registry MC-DAG-Prod-01
- Compute: Spark on managed clusters (batch), SQL pushdown on governed warehouses
- Storage: Object storage for staging; governed warehouse zones for curated layers
- Logging: Centralized log index ETL-Core-Prod, retention 180 days
- Metrics: Enterprise monitoring platform (dashboards prefixed DD-Board-ETL-Prod-###)
- Alerting: Notification router integrated with On-Call schedules (PD services PD-SVC-ETL-PROD-01/02)
- Ticketing: ServiceNow (incident INC, change CHG, problem PRB)

Objectives and success criteria
- Reliability: High signal quality for job success/failure, end-to-end latency, and data completeness across daily and intraday cycles.
- Observability: Traceability from alert to pipeline, dataset, owner team, and last change record.
- Consistency: Uniform naming standards for metrics and tags across all managed DAGs and jobs.
- Business alignment: Data freshness and completeness indicators available in time for Finance and Risk cutoffs.
- Cost awareness: Routine review of resource consumption signals to inform capacity planning (non-exhaustive, descriptive).

Stakeholders and roles
- Data Platform SRE (DPSRE): Platform-level health indicators, orchestration metrics, and alert channel stewardship.
- Enterprise Data Engineering (EDE): Job-level monitoring, data quality rule registration, pipeline ownership in inventory.
- Operations Command Center (OCC): Daily health reviews, first-line interpretation of alerts, status consolidations.
- Finance Data Stewardship (FDS): Business validation signals for close activities; source-of-truth attestations.
- Risk Analytics Technology (RAT): Risk model feed completeness checks and cut-off windows.
- Compliance Data Oversight (CDO): Monitoring of controls related to regulatory datasets (descriptive only).

Parameter set — Primary monitoring channels (Prod snapshot, 2026-07-19T06:30:00Z)

Systems and tooling overview
Monitoring for ETL pipelines relies on a standardized tag model (application, pipeline_id, dataset, domain, env, owner) to unify signals across orchestration, compute, and quality layers. Dashboards aggregate runtime statistics (start lag, duration distributions, success ratio, retry counts), while alert rules track adherence to committed windows. OCC performs daily sign-offs using a consolidated view of pipelines tagged as Finance Close critical, and EDE maintains the mapping of pipelines to business processes in the inventory repository. All changes to alert thresholds follow the bank’s change management process and are reflected in the dashboard annotations for auditability.

Page 2 — Pipeline Landscape, Identifiers, and Alert Taxonomy

Pipeline landscape and identifiers
Meridian Capital maintains a canonical naming convention to simplify monitoring and reporting. Each pipeline identifier encodes business domain, dataset, and frequency, ensuring consistent correlation across metrics, logs, and tickets. The convention is descriptive and minimizes ambiguity during cross-team reviews.

Parameter set — Identifier schema
- Format: ETL_{DOMAIN}_{DATASET}_{FREQUENCY}
- Domains (examples): FIN, RISK, TRSY, RET
- Datasets (examples): GL, PD, LCR, CARDS
- Frequencies: INTRADAY, HOURLY, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY
- Tag set (minimum): application=etl, pipeline_id, dataset, domain, env, owner, criticality

Primary workflow categories
- Ingestion: Source extracts from governed upstreams into staging zones using standardized connectors and manifests.
- Transformation: Batch transformations executed on managed compute or warehouse pushdown with lineage annotations.
- Load: Materialization into curated layers and downstream marts, with row-count and checksum signals emitted.
- Data quality: Rule evaluations for freshness, completeness, and referential consistency; results surfaced as metrics and dashboard tiles.
- Business validation: Finance and Risk steward attestations captured as status flags aligned to cutoff calendars.

Metrics dictionary (extract; see Appendix C for comprehensive list)
- job_start_lag_seconds: Time difference between scheduled start and actual start of a job within a pipeline.
- job_duration_seconds: Elapsed processing time for a job execution.
- pipeline_success_ratio: Ratio of successful jobs to total jobs in the last defined window.
- data_freshness_lag_seconds: Age of the most recent successful load compared to expected data timestamp.
- row_count_delta_ratio: Proportional change in loaded row counts relative to a rolling baseline.
- dq_rule_pass_ratio: Percentage of data quality rules passing in the last run.
- retry_count: Number of task retries observed for the current execution window.

SLO catalog excerpt (Prod, 2026-07 snapshot)

- ETL_TRSY_LIQ_WEEKLY: Completion by Monday 12:00 UTC; data completeness flagged for all inputs; dq_rule_pass_ratio >= 0.97; monthly target: 99% adherence.

Parameter set — Alert taxonomy (KB-ETL-2147-aligned)

- Severity P2: High priority degradation risking SLO breach for critical datasets; OCC summary flag on DD-Board-ETL-Prod-042.
- Severity P3: Non-critical schedule drift or transient freshness variance; tracked in weekly OCC summary.
- Severity P4: Informational deviations and post-change annotations; consolidated in monthly review.
