2. Monitoring Architecture Overview

This section summarizes the end-to-end monitoring surfaces that provide operational visibility into the Enterprise ETL Platform (Program ID: ETL-PF-01). The objective is to ensure consistent observability across source ingestion, transformation orchestration, quality controls, and downstream publishing. The ETL Platform is treated as a business-critical service, with monitoring aligned to service-level objectives (SLOs) and capacity/volume baselines. The architecture emphasizes signal layering: component health (infrastructure, orchestration), pipeline runtime (task/job metrics), data contract adherence (schema, lineage), and business-facing data reliability (freshness, completeness, accuracy).

All monitors are cataloged within the Monitoring Registry (REG-MON-ETL v2.3). Changes to monitors, alert thresholds, or routing rules are governed via standardized change tickets (CHG-ETL- series) and require approval from the ETL Ops Duty Manager and SRE On-Call.

Component Inventory (Monitoring Scope)

- Scope includes ingestion connectors, batch schedulers, transformation jobs, quality gates, and publishing endpoints.
- Component criticality ratings are aligned to the Revenue Risk Index (RRI) and Regulatory Reporting importance.

Component Inventory Table — ETL-PF-01

- Component ID: SRC-FX-ING-01
  Owner: Data Integration Team (DI-NA)
  Criticality: High
  Uptime SLO: 99.9% monthly
  Primary Monitors: Availability, Throughput, Backlog Depth
  Monitor IDs (Registry): MON-AV-1203; MON-TH-2210; MON-BL-3308

- Component ID: ORC-BAT-CTL-02
  Owner: ETL Operations (ETLOPS)
  Criticality: High
  Uptime SLO: 99.95% monthly
  Primary Monitors: Scheduler Heartbeat, Queue Latency, Task Failure Rate
  Monitor IDs (Registry): MON-HB-1407; MON-QL-2712; MON-TF-4419

- Component ID: TRF-CRD-RSK-07
  Owner: Credit Risk Data Engineering (CRDE)
  Criticality: High
  Uptime SLO: 99.9% monthly
  Primary Monitors: Job Duration, Row-Level Error Rate, Checkpoint Success
  Monitor IDs (Registry): MON-DU-3516; MON-ER-3619; MON-CK-3721

- Component ID: DQ-GATE-CUR-01
  Owner: Data Quality Office (DQO)
  Criticality: High

- Component ID: PBL-MART-LQ-09
  Owner: Analytics Publishing (APUB)
  Criticality: Medium
  Uptime SLO: 99.5% monthly
  Primary Monitors: Publish Latency, Consumer Readiness, Version Consistency
  Monitor IDs (Registry): MON-PL-5207; MON-CR-5210; MON-VC-5218

Signal Taxonomy

Signals are grouped to ensure consistent thresholding and incident routing. Each signal category includes standard labels: component_id, environment (prod/non-prod), dataset, owner_team, and severity_candidate.

- Availability: Binary liveness and health checks for schedulers, agents, and endpoints.
- Latency: End-to-end and segment durations relative to SLOs; includes schedule delay and run time.
- Volume: Record counts, file counts, and bytes processed; measured against rolling baselines.
- Quality: Completeness, uniqueness, validity against data contracts; summarized via percentile scores.
- Schema Drift: Additions, removals, or type changes in inbound structures; contract variance is flagged.
- Backlog: Queue depth and unprocessed work units relative to time-based drains.
- Freshness: Age of latest successful partition/publication versus consumer expectations.

Signal Mapping Table — Monitoring Registry (Excerpt)

- Signal: Availability
  Metric Source: Orchestration Heartbeat; Health Probe
  Threshold Boundary: < 1 missed heartbeat within 5 min
  Sampling Window: 5 min rolling
  Escalation Group: SRE Primary (SRE-ETL-OC)

- Signal: Latency
  Metric Source: Job Start/End Markers; Schedule Delay
  Threshold Boundary: p95 runtime ≤ baseline + 20%
  Sampling Window: 24 hr rolling, hourly refresh
  Escalation Group: ETL Operations (ETLOPS)

- Signal: Volume
  Metric Source: Ingestion Counts; Byte Totals
  Threshold Boundary: −15% to +30% versus 14-day median
  Sampling Window: Daily, with intraday checkpoints
  Escalation Group: Data Integration (DI-NA)

- Signal: Quality
  Metric Source: DQ Assertions; Rule Scores
  Threshold Boundary: Composite DQ Score ≥ 98.5
  Sampling Window: Per-batch evaluation
  Escalation Group: Data Quality Office (DQO)

- Signal: Schema Drift
  Metric Source: Contract Validator
  Threshold Boundary: Zero unapproved breaking changes
  Sampling Window: Per-ingest event
  Escalation Group: Data Contract Stewards (DCS)

KPI and SLO Definitions

Service reliability is measured via KPIs anchored to business outcomes. The following KPIs inform the alerting thresholds and incident severities. All SLOs are set for the production environment (ENV: PROD-NA-1) and reviewed quarterly.

- KPI: Consumer Publish Latency

Prepared by: SRE Platforms with ETL Operations

3. Alert Routing and Severity Model

Alerting adheres to a standardized severity model calibrated to customer impact, data timeliness, and regulatory considerations. Severity levels determine notification channels, response time objectives, and status reporting cadence. All production alerts must reference a Monitor ID and include required labels (component_id, dataset, environment, owner_team, severity_candidate, region).

Severity Matrix

- SEV-1 (Critical): Material impact on regulatory or revenue-sensitive datasets; missed freshness SLO p99; complete pipeline halt without workaround.
  Response Objective: Engage Incident Command within 5 minutes; executive notification required.
  Routing: SRE Primary + ETLOPS + Data Leadership bridge.
  Ticket: Auto-create Major Incident (MI) — prefix MC-DATA-MI-.

  Response Objective: Acknowledge within 30 minutes; monitor and mitigate.
  Routing: Owning team; informational to SRE.
  Ticket: Service Request or Problem (SR/PRB) upon recurrence.

- SEV-4 (Low/Info): Transient anomalies, known maintenance windows, expected seasonal effects.
  Response Objective: No immediate action; catalog for trend analysis.

Page 5: Data Freshness and Latency Monitors

Overview
Data freshness and latency monitors verify that pipeline outputs arrive within agreed service windows and reflect recent source activity. This section defines canonical metrics, environment parameters, monitoring thresholds, and the routine review cadence adopted by Data Platform Operations (DPO) and Enterprise Data Engineering (EDE). The objective is to consistently detect delayed or stale datasets ahead of downstream BI refreshes and intraday risk computations.

Key Definitions
- Freshness: Current UTC time minus the maximum available business event timestamp (watermark) in the target dataset.
- Latency: Duration between the scheduled pipeline start and the time the last committed record for the target partition is available in the warehouse.
- SLA Window: The time interval during which the dataset must be available for dependent consumers.

Page 6: Volume and Schema Drift Monitoring

Overview
Volume and schema drift monitors ensure that data completeness and structural consistency remain within expected bounds for each dataset and ingest feed. Volume monitors detect anomalous record counts, partition sparsity, or distributional changes. Schema drift monitors detect column additions/removals, data type changes, and primary key constraint violations. This section covers baseline calculations, anomaly parameters, review cadence, and the decision matrix for triage.

Signal Definitions
- Volume Delta (%): Relative difference between observed record_count and expected baseline for the same business date and comparable weekday/season.
- Null Ratio (%): Proportion of nulls in critical fields compared to baseline tolerance.
- Duplicate Rate (%): Fraction of records breaching declared uniqueness constraints.
- Schema Change: Detected modification to column set or types versus the catalog contract at runtime.
- Key Violation: Existence of duplicate business keys in the output partition.

|--------------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| Baseline Window                | 28 days rolling        | 21 days rolling        | Seasonality-aware (weekday weighting)                |
| Sensitivity (Z-score)          | 2.5                    | 3.0                    | Lower value = higher sensitivity                     |
| Minimum Counts (records)       | 10,000                 | 2,000                  | Avoids spurious alerts on small partitions           |
| Null Ratio Tolerance           | +2.0 p.p.              | +3.5 p.p.              | Absolute percentage point delta vs baseline          |
| Duplicate Rate Tolerance       | +0.25 p.p.             | +0.50 p.p.             | Applies to business keys                             |
| Suppression Window (cooldown)  | 45 minutes             | 30 minutes             | Prevents alert storms for the same root cause        |
| Change Ticket Linkage Required | Yes                    | Yes                    | Schema changes require prior CHG reference           |

Section 4. Alert Taxonomy, Thresholds, and Routing

Meridian Capital’s ETL pipeline monitoring is governed by a shared taxonomy to ensure consistent detection, triage, and reporting across data domains. This section enumerates alert dimensions, severity thresholds, routing logic, and maintenance exceptions applied by Data Platform Operations (DPO) in partnership with Enterprise Data Engineering (EDE), Risk Data Services (RDS), and SRE Observability (SRE‑O). All thresholds are calibrated to support business SLAs and data freshness SLOs without generating unnecessary noise. Changes to thresholds and routes require approval via the Data Reliability Change Advisory Board (DR‑CAB).

Monitoring dimensions and associated metric identifiers are standardized to enable aligned dashboards and comparative analytics across pipeline families.

  Metric ID: etl.errors.rate

Section 4.2 ETL SLA Breach Triage Playbook (Non-Outage)

Scope and Intent
This playbook defines the standard triage sequence when an ETL pipeline exhibits elevated latency without hard failure, potentially risking but not yet breaching daily service-level commitments. It applies to PROD ETL workloads tagged etl_core=true and data products with published SLAs (Ref: SLO-ETL-2026). The playbook is designed to minimize time-to-diagnosis while ensuring consistent stakeholder communication.

Entry Criteria
- Alert: ALERT-ETL-INGEST-LATENCY-HIGH fired in PROD AND
- SLA Window: within 120 minutes of an SLA checkpoint OR
- Observed: p95 latency > threshold for ≥15 minutes

Exit Criteria
- p95 latency stabilized below threshold for two consecutive windows OR
- Controlled mitigation in place and downstream stakeholders notified OR
- Incident escalated to Major Incident process (not covered here)

Standard Triage Steps (RunOps)
Step 1
- Action: Acknowledge alert; confirm dataset(s), job ID(s), and environment.
- Owner: EDE On-Call
- Target Time: ≤5 minutes
- Output: Incident opened if not existing (INC-YYYY-XXXXX).

Step 2
- Action: Review ETL Latency Overview (PROD) — Dashboard ID DB-ETL-OVW-03.
- Owner: EDE On-Call
- Target Time: ≤7 minutes
- Output: Identify whether impact is localized (single dataset/job) or systemic.

Step 3
- Action: Correlate upstream indicators (upstream_source_status, arrival_count_last_15m).
- Owner: EDE On-Call with POG support
- Target Time: ≤10 minutes
- Output: Classification tag applied: upstream_delay | capacity_pressure | metadata_ops.

Step 4
- Action: Check work queue depth and recent batch counts for affected pipeline(s).
- Owner: EDE On-Call
- Target Time: ≤10 minutes
- Output: Determine if queuing is increasing, stable, or clearing.

Step 5
- Action: Validate maintenance/release windows in CAL-ETL-REL-2026.
- Owner: POG
- Target Time: ≤5 minutes
- Output: Maintenance correlation confirmed or ruled out.

Step 6
- Action: Post initial status note to stakeholders.
- Owner: Incident Owner (EDE)
- Target Time: ≤20 minutes from alert
- Output: Status includes scope, preliminary cause, next update timebox.

Step 7
- Action: Implement low-risk mitigations aligned with runbook KB-ETL-0012 (e.g., queue prioritization for at-risk dataset).
- Owner: EDE On-Call
- Target Time: ≤25 minutes
- Output: Mitigation status recorded in incident.

Step 8
- Action: Monitor p95 trend for two consecutive windows.
- Owner: EDE On-Call
- Target Time: Ongoing
- Output: Stabilization confirmed or further action required.

Step 9
- Action: If latency persists and SLA checkpoint approaches (<60 minutes), engage Secondary and Duty Manager per EP-ETL-02.
- Owner: EDE On-Call
- Target Time: As threshold approaches
- Output: Escalation noted in incident.

Step 10
- Action: Upon stabilization, record timeline, cause classification, and any adjustments applied.
- Owner: Incident Owner
- Target Time: Within 60 minutes of resolution
- Output: Incident closure summary.

Escalation Matrix Reference
- Policy: EP-ETL-02
- Primary On-Call: EDE RunOps (24x7)
- Secondary: Data Reliability Engineer (06:00-22:00 ET)

Page 12: Metric Baselines, Data Freshness, and Synthetics

Overview

Baseline Configuration Principles (Ref: STD-ETL-MET-02)
- Rolling Window: 28-day lookback aligned by weekday to accommodate trading and finance calendars.
- Aggregation: Median and interquartile range (IQR) used to reduce sensitivity to spikes.
- Deviations: Anomalies flagged when observation deviates beyond dynamic bands (IQR*1.5 or 3σ proxy) sustained over a defined duration.
- Seasonality Adjusters: U.S. market holidays and month-end/quarter-end markers applied to prevent predictable spikes from generating noise.
